417	/// A single Workrooms View tab chip: a leading glyph, the project name, then run / unread / active
418	/// styling. A workroom chip leads with a cube glyph and trails its own name in secondary text; a root
419	/// chip leads with a house glyph (its branch is dropped from the chip; it lives in the inspector). The
420	/// title is capped so a long project or workroom name tail-truncates instead of stretching the chip
421	/// (mirrors `TerminalTabChip`); the tooltip carries the full title AND the path, so a truncated chip
422	/// still reveals its whole name and two same-named workrooms across projects stay distinct. Reads the
423	/// store for unread + run-command state; the bar wraps it with the gestures.
424	private struct WorkroomTabChip: View {
425	  let sid: SidebarID
426	  let target: TerminalTarget
427	  let isActive: Bool
428	  let isHovered: Bool
429	  let isDragging: Bool
430	  /// Draw a hairline on the leading edge, separating two adjacent idle tabs (computed by the bar).
431	  let showLeadingSeparator: Bool
432	
433	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
434	  @EnvironmentObject var notifications: NotificationCenterStore
435	  @EnvironmentObject var terminals: TerminalSessions
436	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
437	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
438	
439	  private var isRoot: Bool {
440	    if case .root = sid { return true }
441	    return false
442	  }
443	
444	  /// The project name — the chip's primary label for every kind of target. A workroom's own name
445	  /// rides alongside as `workroomName` (secondary text); a root is marked by its house glyph.
446	  private var primaryLabel: String {
447	    switch sid {
448	    case .workroom(let project, _), .root(let project), .project(let project):
449	      return (project as NSString).lastPathComponent
450	    }
451	  }
452	
453	  /// A workroom's own name (nil for a root/project) — rendered as trailing secondary text. Resolves

9	/// Pure drag-to-reorder math, shared by the terminal tab strip (`TerminalTabStrip`) and the
10	/// Workrooms tab bar (`WorkroomTabBar`, issue #23). Lifted out of `TerminalTabStrip` so the index
11	/// resolution and gap offsets are unit-testable without a view, and the two strips can't drift.
12	///
13	/// Operates on **position-indexed** chip widths (`widths[i]` is the natural width of the chip at
14	/// position `i`), so it's agnostic to what the chips are — terminal tabs (`UUID`) or workroom
15	/// targets (`String`). The caller maps its own model to a `[CGFloat]` before calling.
16	enum TabReorder {
17	  /// Where the dragged chip lands given its current translation: walk outward from `draggedIndex`,
18	  /// crossing each neighbour once the drag passes that neighbour's half-width (chip width +
19	  /// `spacing`). Reaches index 0 and the last slot.
20	  static func dropTargetIndex(
21	    widths: [CGFloat], draggedIndex di: Int, translation: CGFloat, spacing: CGFloat
22	  ) -> Int {
23	    var idx = di
24	    if translation > 0 {
25	      var accumulated: CGFloat = 0
26	      var j = di + 1
27	      while j < widths.count {
28	        let span = widths[j] + spacing
29	        if translation > accumulated + span / 2 {
30	          idx = j
31	          accumulated += span
32	          j += 1
33	        } else {
34	          break
35	        }
36	      }
37	    } else if translation < 0 {
38	      var accumulated: CGFloat = 0
39	      var j = di - 1
40	      while j >= 0 {
41	        let span = widths[j] + spacing
42	        if -translation > accumulated + span / 2 {
43	          idx = j
44	          accumulated += span
45	          j -= 1
46	        } else {
47	          break
48	        }
49	      }
50	    }
51	    return idx
52	  }
53	
54	  /// Horizontal shift for a non-dragged chip at `index` so the row opens a gap at the drop `target`.
55	  /// `amount` is the dragged chip's width plus inter-chip spacing.
56	  static func gapShift(index: Int, draggedIndex: Int?, target: Int?, amount: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
57	    guard let di = draggedIndex, let ti = target else { return 0 }
58	    if di < ti, index > di, index <= ti { return -amount }  // dragging right: slide left
59	    if di > ti, index >= ti, index < di { return amount }  // dragging left: slide right
60	    return 0
61	  }

90	
91	/// The overflow decision for a horizontal tab strip (issue #129): does the *inline* layout — the chip
92	/// run with the "+" hugging the last chip — still fit the width available to it? When it doesn't, the
93	/// trailing controls lift out of the scroller and pin at its trailing edge, so the "+" is always
94	/// reachable.
95	enum TabStripOverflow {
96	  /// Natural width of a chip run: every chip plus the inter-chip spacing.
97	  static func runWidth(_ widths: [CGFloat], spacing: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
98	    guard !widths.isEmpty else { return 0 }
99	    return widths.reduce(0, +) + spacing * CGFloat(widths.count - 1)
100	  }
101	
102	  /// Whether the trailing controls must pin.
103	  ///
104	  /// Takes **only** quantities that are independent of where those controls currently sit, so the
105	  /// answer cannot depend on the layout it selects: the predicate has one fixed point and cannot
106	  /// oscillate as the window resizes. There is deliberately no `isPinned` parameter — a
107	  /// "scroll content vs viewport" comparison *would* oscillate, because lifting the controls out
108	  /// shrinks the content and the viewport by different amounts, leaving a band of widths that pins,
109	  /// then fits, then pins.
110	  ///
111	  /// - Parameters:
112	  ///   - runWidth: measured width of the whole chip run **including the trailing divider and its
113	  ///     pads** — the divider lives inside the measured run and is toggled by opacity, never removed,
114	  ///     so it is always laid out. Passing a chips-only width would let the boundary tests pass while
115	  ///     the rendered threshold sits a few points off.
116	  ///   - add: the trailing controls' intrinsic width, without any positioning pad.
117	  ///   - available: width the strip has for the chips + controls (its own width minus any
118	  ///     fixed-size sibling such as the per-tab toolbar).
119	  ///   - leadingInset: the row's leading inset (4pt in a workroom split, else 8pt).
120	  ///   - inlineAddLead: gap between the run and the controls while inline (spacing + their own pad).
121	  static func pinsControls(
122	    runWidth: CGFloat, add: CGFloat, available: CGFloat,
123	    leadingInset: CGFloat, inlineAddLead: CGFloat, gutter: CGFloat = TabStripMetrics.gutter,
124	    epsilon: CGFloat = TabStripMetrics.epsilon
125	  ) -> Bool {
126	    // Nothing measured yet (first layout pass): render inline. Every input is branch-independent, so
127	    // the correction that follows happens exactly once — it can't become a loop.
128	    guard available > 0, runWidth > 0, add > 0 else { return false }
129	    let inlineWidth = leadingInset + runWidth + inlineAddLead + add + gutter
130	    return inlineWidth > available + epsilon
131	  }
132	}
133	
134	/// Geometry of a split group's contiguous chip run within a strip — the `x`/`width` of the rounded
135	/// bracket drawn around the members (issue #3). Lifted out of `TerminalTabStrip.splitRunRect` so the
136	/// arithmetic is unit-testable without a view, and so it shares one summation with
137	/// `TabStripOverflow.runWidth` instead of carrying a second copy of it.
138	enum TabStripSplitRun {
139	  /// - Parameters:
140	  ///   - widths: position-indexed chip widths (`widths[i]` is the chip at position `i`).
141	  ///   - memberIndices: positions of the group's members. Guaranteed contiguous by the caller's
142	  ///     display order; only the first and last are used, so a stray gap is spanned rather than
143	  ///     rejected.
144	  ///   - spacing: the strip's inter-chip spacing.
145	  /// - Returns: `nil` when there's no real split (fewer than two members) or the indices are out of
146	  ///   range — both mean "draw no bracket".
147	  static func rect(widths: [CGFloat], memberIndices: [Int], spacing: CGFloat)
148	    -> (x: CGFloat, width: CGFloat)?
149	  {
150	    guard memberIndices.count >= 2,
151	      let first = memberIndices.min(), let last = memberIndices.max(),
152	      first >= 0, last < widths.count
153	    else { return nil }
154	    // x: everything before the first member, chips + the spacing that follows each of them.
155	    var x: CGFloat = 0
156	    for i in 0..<first { x += widths[i] + spacing }
157	    // width: the members' own chips, plus the spacing *between* them (one fewer gap than chips).
158	    var width: CGFloat = 0
159	    for i in first...last { width += widths[i] }
160	    width += spacing * CGFloat(last - first)
161	    return (x, width)
162	  }
163	}

1	import Defaults
2	import SwiftUI

4	/// The horizontal tab strip above a target's terminal: a chip per terminal tab, a "+" to open a
5	/// new one, and the drag interactions — reorder within the strip, or drag a chip down into a pane
6	/// to split (issue #3). Fully owns the reorder drag state; the drop-into-pane wiring is shared with
7	/// the pane content, so `WorkroomTerminalsView` passes a `chipPaneDrag` binding (the live preview the
8	/// pane tree renders) plus `localize`/`dropTarget` closures that resolve a cursor point against the
9	/// pane area (which only the coordinator knows the frame of).
10	///
11	/// The "+" is **adaptive** (issue #129): while the tabs fit it sits inline, hugging the last chip;
12	/// once they overflow it lifts out of the scroller and pins at the strip's trailing edge, so it's
13	/// never scrolled out of reach. The scroller's trailing edge carries an alpha ramp in that state, so
14	/// a clipped chip dissolves instead of being cut mid-glyph. The decision itself is
15	/// `TabStripOverflow.pinsControls`, wired up by the shared `OverflowingTabScroller` (which
16	/// `WorkroomTabBar` uses too, so the two strips can't drift).
17	struct TerminalTabStrip: View {
18	  let tabs: [TerminalTab]
19	  let activeID: TerminalTab.ID?
20	  let target: TerminalTarget
21	  @ObservedObject var sessions: TerminalSessions
22	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
23	  @EnvironmentObject var notifications: NotificationCenterStore
24	  @EnvironmentObject var agentManager: TerminalAgentManager
25	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
26	  /// The tab whose ✦ agent popover is open.
27	  @State private var agentPopoverTab: TerminalTab.ID?
28	  /// Global default diff layout — the toolbar's mode toggle shows it as active until this tab gets a
29	  /// per-tab override (`TerminalTab.diffViewModeOverride`).
30	  @Default(.diffViewMode) private var defaultDiffViewMode
31	
32	  /// The live drop-into-pane preview, shared with `PaneTreeView` via the coordinator.
33	  @Binding var chipPaneDrag: PaneDragState?
34	  /// The pane-local point for a chip drag at a global location, or nil when the cursor is still over
35	  /// the strip (→ a reorder, not a drop-into-pane). Owned by the coordinator (needs the pane frame).
36	  let localize: (CGPoint) -> CGPoint?
37	  /// Where a chip dropped at a global location lands (pane + edge), or nil if it isn't over a pane.
38	  let dropTarget: (CGPoint) -> (tab: TerminalTab.ID, edge: PaneEdge)?
39	
40	  @State private var hoveredTab: TerminalTab.ID?
41	  @State private var addHovering = false
42	  /// The last chip click (id + time), so a quick second click on the same chip promotes a preview
43	  /// content tab to persisted without delaying the eager first-click select (#66).
44	  @State private var lastChipClick: ChipClick?
45	
46	  // Drag-to-reorder. The tab order is *frozen* for the duration of a drag: the dragged
47	  // chip simply follows the cursor (its slot never moves, so it can't jump), and the
48	  // other chips slide aside to open a gap. The reorder is committed once, on drop.
49	  @State private var draggingID: TerminalTab.ID?
50	  @State private var dragTranslation: CGFloat = 0
51	  @State private var widths: [TerminalTab.ID: CGFloat] = [:]
52	
53	  private let tabSpacing: CGFloat = 4
54	  /// The strip's own right inset. Lives here rather than on `tabToolbar` (which renders *nothing* when
55	  /// there's no active tab) so a pinned "+" is never flush against the pane edge.
56	  private static let stripTrailingInset: CGFloat = 4
57	
58	  /// The strip's leading inset, lining the leftmost tab up with the terminal panel below it: the pane
59	  /// tree is inset 2pt inside the workroom's card and each pane leaf pads another 2pt.
60	  private static let leadingInset: CGFloat = 4
61	
62	  var body: some View {
63	    // Resolve the drag once per layout: which tab is dragging, and where it would land.
64	    let draggedIndex = draggingID.flatMap { id in tabs.firstIndex { $0.id == id } }
65	    // While dragging a chip down into a pane, the strip stops opening a reorder gap.
66	    let dropIndex =
67	      chipPaneDrag != nil
68	      ? nil
69	      : draggedIndex.map { dropTargetIndex(tabs, draggedIndex: $0, translation: dragTranslation) }
70	    let draggedWidth = draggingID.flatMap { widths[$0] } ?? 0
71	    // Members of the split group (≥2), so a grouped chip's selected pill can inset itself to sit
72	    // *inside* the `splitWell` bracket rather than overrunning it.
73	    let groupMembers = splitMemberSet
74	
75	    // `spacing` is the gutter between the scroller region and the per-tab toolbar, and it has to be a
76	    // real gutter rather than leftover slack. `OverflowingTabScroller`'s pinned "+" rides a
77	    // `safeAreaInset(edge: .trailing)`, which puts its `spacing:` between the CHIPS and the "+" and
78	    // leaves the "+" itself flush with the scroller's trailing edge — so at `spacing: 0` a pinned "+"
79	    // abutted the first toolbar button exactly (measured: both at x=1123), which is symptom 1 of issue
80	    // #129. It went unnoticed because at the old strip width the default fixture's tabs still fit
81	    // INLINE, where the gap happened to be leftover slack; issue #139's card geometry narrowed the strip
82	    // enough to pin, and `TabStripOverflowUITests.testPinnedAddButtonKeepsGutterFromToolbar` caught it.
83	    HStack(spacing: TabStripMetrics.gutter) {
84	      // The scrolling chips plus the adaptive "+" (issue #129), assembled by the shared
85	      // `OverflowingTabScroller`. The width it measures for the overflow predicate is the scroller's
86	      // own: it's the flexible child beside the `fixedSize` toolbar, so it already equals "strip minus
87	      // toolbar" (and the full strip when there's no active tab and the toolbar renders nothing).
88	      OverflowingTabScroller(
89	        leadingInset: Self.leadingInset, spacing: tabSpacing,
90	        inlineLead: TabStripMetrics.inlineAddLead,
91	        // Scroll the focused tab into view on selection (issue #129 follow-up); suspended mid-drag,
92	        // like the reorder gap animation below.
93	        scrollTarget: activeID, scrollSuspended: draggingID != nil
94	      ) { overflowing in
95	        chipRun(
96	          tabs, draggedIndex: draggedIndex, dropIndex: dropIndex, draggedWidth: draggedWidth,
97	          groupMembers: groupMembers, overflowing: overflowing)
98	      } controls: {
99	        addTerminalButton
100	      }
101	      // Per-current-tab actions (issue #72), pinned to the strip's right edge as a fixed-size layout
102	      // sibling of the scrolling tabs — so the chip area yields first in a cramped split pane and the
103	      // toolbar never overlaps the chips. An overflowing strip's "+" now sits between the two, pinned
104	      // to the scroller's trailing edge (issue #129). The remove-from-split ✕ used to sit to its
105	      // right; it now lives in the workroom-split group title bar (issue #110).
106	      tabToolbar
107	    }
108	    // No top padding: the strip sits flush at the top of the detail pane so the terminal tabs align
109	    // with the top of the sidebar (the pane's own top inset is dropped too — see `WorkroomPaneLeaf`).
110	    .padding(.top, 0)
111	    // Flush with the content below — the active tab's `bg` fill bridges the panel→bg colour step so
112	    // the strip reads as part of the terminal panel (Chrome-style). No bottom gap.
113	    .padding(.bottom, 0)
114	    .padding(.trailing, Self.stripTrailingInset)
115	  }
116	
117	  /// The chips themselves plus the hairline that sets the inline "+" apart — everything that scrolls

---
name: macapp-xcuitest-automation-wedge
description: "macapp XCUITest runs failing \"Timed out while enabling automation mode\" = wedged automation subsystem, not test code; often clears on its own after a pause — retry before resetting the login session."
metadata:

---

`make app-uitest` / `xcodebuild ... -scheme WorkroomAppUITests test` failing with
`WorkroomAppUITests-Runner encountered an error (The test runner failed to initialize for UI
testing. (Underlying Error: Timed out while enabling automation mode.))` is an **environmental
wedge of the macOS UI-automation subsystem**, NOT a code failure — it fails at runner init before
any test code runs, and `xcodebuild ... build` + `make app-test` (unit target, in-process, no
automation runner) still pass.

Triggered by hammering many XCUITest launches in one session (and/or heavy `screencapture`). No
stuck `WorkroomAppUITests-Runner` / `Workroom Dev` / `testmanagerd` process to kill — `ps` is
clean.

**It can clear on its own.** 2026-07-26: wedged (1 attempt), then ~2h later — after an unrelated
stretch of building, unit tests and editing, no login-session reset — the same command ran clean
and the full 104-test suite completed. So: **retry after a gap before escalating.** A login session
reset (log out/in, same class of remedy as [[macapp-swbbuildservice-wedge]]) is still the fix when
it persists; an earlier session saw 3× identical failures back-to-back with no recovery, so
immediate retries are the thing that doesn't work.

Second confirmation, 2026-07-31 (issue #139): wedged mid-session, and the cheap way to prove it was
environmental was re-running a test the change did NOT touch
(`WorkroomsViewUITests/testActiveWorkroomShowsATab`) — identical failure ⇒ stop debugging the diff.
Cleared later in the SAME session after nothing but elapsed time and intervening builds/unit runs,
and then 58 XCUITests ran green. So the untouched-test check is the first move, and retry is the
second; a login reset stayed unnecessary both times.

Third confirmation, 2026-08-08 (issue #46): the same suite passed at 00:46, wedged at 09:40 on the
first run of the morning (so an overnight gap does NOT prevent it), and cleared on a plain retry a
few minutes later with no login reset and no processes to kill — `ps` was clean both times. Retry
really is the first move; three occurrences now, zero login resets needed.

Unit tests (`make app-test`) are a valid green signal meanwhile.

4	/// git-backed `VCSProviding`, over SwiftGitX (libgit2). Maps `SwiftGitX.*` types into the app-native
5	/// models. Pure Swift — no Rust involved for git.

7	/// Three reads reach *past* SwiftGitX, all on raw libgit2 (see each type's doc): push state via
8	/// `GitGraph`, because SwiftGitX cannot express the commit RANGE that "not on origin yet" is; commit
9	/// diffs via `GitCommitDiff`, because rename detection has to run on a live `git_diff` and
10	/// SwiftGitX's `Diff` is already materialized and freed by the time we see it; and the working tree's
11	/// ± line counts via `GitDiffStats`, because SwiftGitX's eager `Diff` materializes every changed line
12	/// into a Swift `String` to derive two integers.
13	///
14	/// Errors are caught untyped (`catch { … "\(error)" }`) on purpose: binding SwiftGitX's typed-throws
15	/// error (`catch let e as SwiftGitXError`) trips a Swift 6 SIL ownership error across the async
16	/// boundary.

18	  func log(root: URL, limit: Int) throws -> VCSHistoryPage {
19	    do {
20	      let repo = try Repository.open(at: root)
21	      // A repo with no commits yet (unborn HEAD) is an empty history, not a failure.
22	      if repo.isHEADUnborn { return VCSHistoryPage(commits: [], reachedEnd: true) }
23	
24	      // Take one extra to learn whether more history exists beyond the page.
25	      let window = Array(try repo.log().prefix(max(0, limit) + 1))
26	      let reachedEnd = window.count <= limit
27	      let decorations = Self.decorations(in: repo)
28	      let page = Array(window.prefix(limit))
29	      // Push state for the whole page in one libgit2 revwalk (`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*`).

31	      // `.unknown`, never a partial answer (a skipped tip could badge a pushed commit as unpushed).
32	      let push = GitGraph.unpushed(root: root, decide: Set(page.map { $0.id.hex }))

34	        Self.map(
35	          $0, refs: decorations[$0.id.hex] ?? [],
36	          pushState: Self.pushState($0.id.hex, in: push))
37	      }
38	      return VCSHistoryPage(
39	        commits: commits, reachedEnd: reachedEnd, pushScope: Self.scope(push?.scope))
40	    } catch {
41	      throw VCSError.io("\(error)")
42	    }
43	  }

262	  /// The working-tree status for the sidebar/Changes badges: changed files (incl. untracked +
263	  /// conflicts), dirty flag, current branch (for CI lookup), and the `git diff HEAD` line counts.
264	  /// Read entirely through libgit2 — no subprocess.
265	  ///
266	  /// Security: this replaces the CLI status read that carried `-c core.fsmonitor=` +
267	  /// `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` hardening against an untrusted repo's config executing a program.
268	  /// libgit2 needs no such flags here: its fsmonitor support is the bool/IPC form (it never spawns a
269	  /// `core.fsmonitor` hook program), and its status/diff don't honor `diff.external`/textconv — so
270	  /// there's no config-driven code-execution surface to neutralise.
271	  func workingStatus(root: URL) throws -> GitWorkingStatus {
272	    do {
273	      let repo = try Repository.open(at: root)
274	      var files: [ChangedFile] = []
275	      var conflicted = false
276	      // Enable rename detection (off by default in libgit2) so a `git mv` reads as one `.renamed`
277	      // entry, matching the CLI porcelain this replaced — not a separate delete + add.
278	      let options: StatusOption = [
279	        .includeUntracked, .recurseUntrackedDirectories, .renamesIndex, .renamesWorkingTree,
280	      ]
281	      for entry in try repo.status(options: options) {
282	        if entry.status.contains(.ignored) || entry.status.contains(.current) { continue }
283	        if entry.status.contains(.conflicted) {
284	          conflicted = true
285	          if let path = Self.statusPath(entry) {
286	            files.append(ChangedFile(path: path, change: .conflicted))
287	          }
288	          continue
289	        }
290	        // Prefer the working-tree delta (unstaged), fall back to the index delta (staged-only).
291	        guard let delta = entry.workingTree ?? entry.index,
292	          let change = Self.change(delta.type), let path = Self.statusPath(entry)
293	        else { continue }
294	        // The pre-move path, for the rename rows the options above enable. Guarded on the delta type
295	        // because libgit2 fills `oldFile` for every delta (it's the HEAD/index side of a plain
296	        // modification too), so an unguarded read would label every row a rename.
297	        let oldPath =
298	          (delta.type == .renamed || delta.type == .copied) ? delta.oldFile.path : nil
299	        files.append(
300	          ChangedFile(path: path, change: change, oldPath: oldPath?.isEmpty == true ? nil : oldPath)
301	        )
302	      }
303	      // Current branch for CI (nil when detached / unborn) — `branch.current` throws when detached.
304	      let branch = (try? repo.branch.current.name)
305	      // `git diff HEAD` line counts, on raw libgit2 rather than a second SwiftGitX `Diff`: deriving them
306	      // from one would materialize every patch line of the whole worktree on every refresh, for two
307	      // integers. See `GitDiffStats`. `nil` (a failed read) means the badge shows no count.
308	      let stats = GitDiffStats.workingTree(root: root)
309	      let (insertions, deletions) = (stats?.insertions, stats?.deletions)
310	      return GitWorkingStatus(
311	        dirty: !files.isEmpty, conflicted: conflicted, files: files, branch: branch,
312	        insertions: insertions, deletions: deletions)
313	    } catch {
314	      throw VCSError.io("\(error)")
315	    }

338	    for (id, names) in tags { map[id, default: []].append(contentsOf: names.sorted()) }

8	import Foundation

11	extension Repository {
12	    /// Creates a patch from the difference between two blobs.
13	    ///
14	    /// - Parameters:
15	    ///   - oldBlob: Blob for old side of patch, or `nil` for empty blob.
16	    ///   - newBlob: Blob for new side of patch, or `nil` for empty blob.
17	    ///
18	    /// - Returns: The created patch.
19	    ///
20	    /// If both blobs are `nil`, the patch will be empty.
21	    ///
22	    /// If you want to create a patch from ``StatusEntry``, using ``patch(from:)`` method
23	    /// for ``StatusEntry/workingTree`` and ``StatusEntry/index`` is recommended.
24	    /// But if you will use this method, be sure the file is staged because workingTree files'
25	    /// ``Diff/Delta/newFile`` side's ``Diff/File/id`` property does not have a valid blob id.
26	    /// So, you have to use ``patch(from:to:)-957bd`` method to create patch for the workingTree file.
27	    /// If the file's status is ``StatusEntry/Status-swift.enum/workingTreeNew`` (aka `untracked`)
28	    /// you should use ``patch(from:to:)-957bd`` method with `nil` oldBlob.
29	    public func patch(from oldBlob: Blob?, to newBlob: Blob?) throws(SwiftGitXError) -> Patch {
30	        let oldBlobPointer: OpaquePointer?
31	        let newBlobPointer: OpaquePointer?
32	
33	        // Get the blob pointers if not nil
34	        oldBlobPointer =
35	            if let oldBlob {
36	                try ObjectFactory.lookupObjectPointer(
37	                    oid: oldBlob.id.raw,
38	                    type: GIT_OBJECT_BLOB,
39	                    repositoryPointer: pointer
40	                )
41	            } else { nil }
42	        defer { git_object_free(oldBlobPointer) }
43	
44	        newBlobPointer =
45	            if let newBlob {
46	                try ObjectFactory.lookupObjectPointer(
47	                    oid: newBlob.id.raw,
48	                    type: GIT_OBJECT_BLOB,
49	                    repositoryPointer: pointer
50	                )
51	            } else { nil }
52	        defer { git_object_free(newBlobPointer) }
53	
54	        // Create the patch object
55	        let patchPointer = try git(operation: .patch) {
56	            var patchPointer: OpaquePointer?
57	            let status = git_patch_from_blobs(&patchPointer, oldBlobPointer, nil, newBlobPointer, nil, nil)
58	            return (patchPointer, status)
59	        }
60	        defer { git_patch_free(patchPointer) }
61	
62	        return Patch(pointer: patchPointer)
63	    }
64	
65	    /// Creates a patch from the difference between a blob and a file.
66	    ///
67	    /// - Parameters:
68	    ///   - blob: Blob for old side of patch, or `nil` for empty blob.
69	    ///   - file: URL of the file for new side of patch.
70	    ///
71	    /// - Returns: The created patch.
72	    public func patch(from blob: Blob?, to file: URL) throws(SwiftGitXError) -> Patch {
73	        // Get the blob pointer if not nil
74	        let blobPointer: OpaquePointer?
75	
76	        blobPointer =
77	            if let blob {
78	                try ObjectFactory.lookupObjectPointer(
79	                    oid: blob.id.raw,
80	                    type: GIT_OBJECT_BLOB,
81	                    repositoryPointer: pointer
82	                )
83	            } else { nil }
84	        defer { git_object_free(blobPointer) }
85	
86	        // Get the new file content
87	        let fileContent: NSData
88	        do {
89	            fileContent = try NSData(contentsOf: file)
90	        } catch {
91	            throw SwiftGitXError(code: .error, category: .filesystem, message: "Failed to read file content")
92	        }
93	
94	        // Create the patch object
95	        let patchPointer = try git(operation: .patch) {
96	            var patchPointer: OpaquePointer?
97	            let status = git_patch_from_blob_and_buffer(
98	                &patchPointer,
99	                blobPointer,
100	                nil,
101	                fileContent.bytes,
102	                fileContent.count,
103	                nil,
104	                nil
105	            )
106	            return (patchPointer, status)
107	        }
108	        defer { git_patch_free(patchPointer) }
109	
110	        return Patch(pointer: patchPointer)
111	    }
112	
113	    /// Creates a patch from given diff delta.
114	    ///
115	    /// - Parameter delta: The diff delta to create the patch from.
116	    ///
117	    /// - Returns: The created patch.
118	    ///
119	    /// This method does not support all diff delta types.
120	    /// It only supports ``Diff/DeltaType/untracked``, ``Diff/DeltaType/added``, and ``Diff/DeltaType/modified`` types,
121	    /// for now.
122	    public func patch(from delta: Diff.Delta) throws(SwiftGitXError) -> Patch? {
123	        // TODO: Complete the all cases
124	        switch delta.type {
125	        case .untracked:
126	            let newFileURL = try workingDirectory.appendingPathComponent(delta.newFile.path)
127	            // Create a patch from an empty blob to the file content
128	            return try patch(from: nil, to: newFileURL)
129	        case .added:
130	            let oldBlobID = delta.oldFile.id
131	            let oldBlob: Blob = try show(id: oldBlobID)
132	
133	            let newBlobID = delta.newFile.id
134	            let newBlob: Blob = try show(id: newBlobID)
135	
136	            // Create a patch from the old blob to the new blob
137	            return try patch(from: oldBlob, to: newBlob)
138	        case .modified, .renamed:
139	            let oldBlobID = delta.oldFile.id
140	            let oldBlob: Blob = try show(id: oldBlobID)
141	
142	            let newFileURL = try workingDirectory.appendingPathComponent(delta.newFile.path)
143	
144	            // Create a patch from the old blob to the file content
145	            return try patch(from: oldBlob, to: newFileURL)
146	        default:
147	            return nil
148	        }
149	    }

content.subject: Fix withTimeout not observing caller's own cancellation

Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. 3	/// What a CI probe decided. `keepPrior` means "don't overwrite the last good value" (a
4	/// transient rate-limit / network blip), so a flaky `gh` doesn't flicker the badge to nothing.
5	enum CIResolution: Equatable, Sendable {
6	  case state(CIState)
7	  case absent  // gh missing/unauth, no remote, no runs, or runs are for a different commit
8	  case keepPrior
9	}
10	
11	/// What a PR probe decided. `keepPrior` (transient rate-limit/network blip) keeps the last good PR
12	/// so a flaky `gh` doesn't flicker the Pull Request section to empty.
13	enum PRResolution: Equatable, Sendable {
14	  case info(PullRequestInfo)
15	  case absent  // gh missing/unauth, no remote, or no PR for the branch
16	  case keepPrior
17	}
18	
19	/// What a PR-checks probe decided (issue #75). `list([])` is a valid "loaded, no checks" result —
20	/// distinct from `absent`. `keepPrior` (transient rate-limit/network blip) keeps the last good list
21	/// so a flaky `gh` doesn't flicker the panel's check rows.
22	enum ChecksResolution: Equatable, Sendable {
23	  case list([CICheck])
24	  case absent  // gh missing/unauth, no remote, or no checks reported
25	  case keepPrior
26	}
27	
28	/// Resolves a workroom's VCS + CI status app-side by shelling to git/jj/gh. App-side (not in
29	/// the `workroom --json` contract) for the same reasons as `BranchResolver`: GUI-only, keeps
30	/// `list` instant, isolates a slow repo to its own row. Stage 1 (`resolveLocal`) is fast/local;
31	/// stage 2 (`resolveCI`) is the slow network call and runs separately so it never blocks the
32	/// dirty dot. Pure parsers are `static` so they're unit-tested without spawning anything.
33	struct WorkroomStatusResolver: Sendable {
34	  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
35	  var timeout: TimeInterval  // local git/jj
36	  var ciTimeout: TimeInterval  // gh (network)
37	  /// Serializes jj working-copy snapshots per project root (see `JJSnapshotGate`) — a project's
38	  /// workrooms share a backing repo, so concurrent snapshots can contend on it.
39	  var gate: JJSnapshotGate
40	
41	  /// How long `resolveJJ` waits its turn behind other same-project jj snapshots, before the row
42	  /// reports `.timeout`. Deliberately larger than `timeout`: with the gate serializing a busy
43	  /// project's workrooms, a healthy repo can sit queued behind several real (not contended)
44	  /// snapshots — this budgets the *wait*, not any single native call (which stays un-timed inside
45	  /// the gate; see `JJSnapshotGate`'s doc on why timing the operation itself would be unsafe).
46	  static let jjGatedWaitTimeout: TimeInterval = 15
47	
48	  init(
49	    runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(), timeout: TimeInterval = 3,
50	    ciTimeout: TimeInterval = 10, gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
51	  ) {
52	    self.runner = runner
53	    self.timeout = timeout
54	    self.ciTimeout = ciTimeout
55	    self.gate = gate
56	  }
57	
58	  /// `-c` overrides prepended to every `git` invocation. A workroom can be a clone of an *untrusted*
59	  /// repo, and the status sweep runs git automatically on load/focus/selection — without this, a
60	  /// repo-local `core.fsmonitor` runs an arbitrary program on a plain `git status`. The diff probe
61	  /// additionally passes `--no-ext-diff`/`--no-textconv` (and the runner unsets `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`)
62	  /// so `diff.external`/textconv config can't execute either. These flags go before the subcommand.
63	  static let gitHardening = ["-c", "core.fsmonitor="]
64	
65	  // MARK: Stage 1 — local VCS status
66	
67	  /// `projectRoot` is the colocated project root (`StatusWorkItem.projectRoot`) — required, not
68	  /// defaulted, so every call site is forced to supply the key `resolveJJ`'s snapshot gate needs;
69	  /// `resolveGit` ignores it (git reads are never gated).
70	  func resolveLocal(path: String, vcs: String, projectRoot: String) async -> WorkroomStatus {
71	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: path) else {
72	      return WorkroomStatus(dirty: nil, failure: .missingPath)
73	    }
74	    switch vcs {
75	    case "git": return await resolveGit(path)
76	    case "jj": return await resolveJJ(path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
77	    default: return WorkroomStatus(dirty: nil, failure: .notRepository)
78	    }
79	  }
80	
81	  /// Which "unknown" badge a typed backend error earns. Pure, so the mapping is unit-tested without
82	  /// a repo.
83	  ///
84	  /// Only the two states a *retry* can clear get their own badge: the working-copy lock being held
85	  /// (`.busy`) and a working copy that moved under the read (`.staleWorkingCopy`) — both raised by
86	  /// the jj core's snapshot, both self-describing in the sidebar tooltip and the Changes panel.
87	  /// Everything else stays `.notRepository`, which is also the honest answer for the common git case:
88	  /// `GitProvider` can't bind SwiftGitX's typed error (a Swift 6 SIL crash — see its doc), so a
89	  /// missing/broken repo arrives as `.io` and must keep reading as "not a repository".
90	  static func failure(for error: VCSError) -> VCSStatusFailure {
91	    switch error {
92	    case .lockContention: return .busy
93	    case .staleSnapshot: return .staleWorkingCopy
94	    case .unsupportedRepo, .notFound, .partialData, .backendVersion, .io: return .notRepository
95	    }
96	  }
97	
98	  private func resolveGit(_ dir: String) async -> WorkroomStatus {
99	    // Read git status structurally through libgit2 (SwiftGitX) instead of shelling `git status` +
100	    // `git diff --shortstat`. `VCSProviding` has no built-in timeout, so bound the (synchronous,
101	    // off-main) read with `withTimeout` — a wedged repo abandons only its own row.
102	    let root = URL(fileURLWithPath: dir, isDirectory: true)
103	    do {
104	      let ws = try await withTimeout(seconds: timeout) {
105	        // `runBlocking` (GCD), NOT `Task.detached`: the cooperative pool is fixed-width and this read
106	        // is fanned out ~5-wide per sweep (`runLocalSweep`), overlapping History/diff/branch reads —
107	        // exactly the burst the `runBlocking` doc flags as the "History loads forever" starvation.
108	        try await runBlocking { try GitProvider().workingStatus(root: root) }
109	      }
110	      return WorkroomStatus(
111	        dirty: ws.dirty, conflicted: ws.conflicted, changedFiles: ws.files,
112	        insertions: ws.insertions, deletions: ws.deletions, branchForCI: ws.branch)
113	    } catch is VCSTimeoutError {
114	      return WorkroomStatus(dirty: nil, failure: .timeout)
115	    } catch let error as VCSError {
116	      return WorkroomStatus(dirty: nil, failure: Self.failure(for: error))
117	    } catch {
118	      return WorkroomStatus(dirty: nil, failure: .notRepository)
119	    }
120	  }

123	    // Read the jj working-copy status structurally through the Rust core (jj-lib): it snapshots `@`
124	    // (so it reflects disk) and returns the `@`/`@-` change sets, the ± line counts and the CI branch

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Workroom VCS + CI status scheduling (issue #24). Split out of `AppStore` (already large) per
4	/// the `AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift` convention. Best-effort / "last checked", NOT real-time:
5	/// statuses refresh on load, on app focus (via reload), on selection (debounced), and never via
6	/// a file watcher in Phase 1. The fan-out across all workrooms is bounded (so 50 workrooms
7	/// don't fork 50 git + 50 gh processes at once); CI is a second, slower stage that never blocks
8	/// the dirty dot, and is gated by a much longer TTL than the local git probe. Three separate lanes
9	/// here (this sweep, `scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh`, `handleWorkroomFileChange`) — plus a fourth
10	/// outside this file, the Changes panel's working-copy diff (`DiffResolver`) — can all reach a jj
11	/// snapshot for the same project concurrently; `JJSnapshotGate` (via `WorkroomStatusResolver`)
12	/// serializes same-project jj snapshots across ALL of them, not just within one lane.
13	extension AppStore {
14	  fileprivate static let localStatusTTL: TimeInterval = 15  // git/jj dirty/changed-files
15	  fileprivate static let ciStatusTTL: TimeInterval = 300  // gh CI (network)
16	  // The `gh auth status` TTL lives in `GitHubAuthCache`, which owns that probe's freshness outright.
17	  fileprivate static let localConcurrency = 5
18	  fileprivate static let ciConcurrency = 2
19	  fileprivate static let selectionDebounce: TimeInterval = 0.3  // arrow-key row cycling coalesce
20	
21	  struct StatusWorkItem: Sendable {
22	    let sid: SidebarID
23	    let path: String
24	    let vcs: String
25	    /// The colocated project root. Equals `path` for the root row; for a workroom it's the parent
26	    /// project's path — where stage-2 `gh` probes run for a jj workspace (which has no `.git`).
27	    let projectRoot: String
28	  }
29	
30	  /// Every root + workroom as a status work item.
31	  func statusWorkItems() -> [StatusWorkItem] {
32	    var items: [StatusWorkItem] = []
33	    for p in projects {
34	      items.append(
35	        StatusWorkItem(sid: .root(project: p.id), path: p.path, vcs: p.vcs, projectRoot: p.path))
36	      for w in p.workrooms {
37	        // A workroom's VCS *type* is its project's (`p.vcs`) — a git project's workrooms are git
38	        // worktrees, a jj project's are jj workspaces. NOT `w.vcsName`, which is the workroom's
39	        // branch/workspace *name* (`workroom/<name>`); passing that as the type made resolveLocal
40	        // fall through to `.notRepository` for every workroom.
41	        items.append(
42	          StatusWorkItem(
43	            sid: .workroom(project: p.id, name: w.name), path: w.path, vcs: p.vcs,
44	            projectRoot: p.path))
45	      }
46	    }
47	    return items
48	  }
49	
50	  /// Sweep every workroom's status. Cancels any in-flight sweep so a slow one can't write stale
51	  /// values over a newer one. `force` ignores the TTLs (e.g. a manual refresh). Two stages:
52	  /// fast local git/jj first, then the slow `gh` CI pass — so the dirty dots land immediately.
53	  func refreshWorkroomStatuses(force: Bool = false) {
54	    // Fixture mode never shells out to git/jj/gh — keep the deterministic seeded status (and let the
55	    // manual Refresh button re-apply it rather than wipe it to "unknown").
56	    if UITestFixture.isActive {
57	      seedFixtureStatuses()
58	      return
59	    }
60	    statusSweepTask?.cancel()
61	    let resolver = statusResolver
62	    let now = Date()
63	    let localTTL = Self.localStatusTTL
64	    let ciTTL = Self.ciStatusTTL
65	    let localItems = statusWorkItems().filter { item in
66	      // Never sweep a workroom whose setup is still writing its worktree (issue: create-time FSEvents
67	      // storm) — even on `force`. Its status is refreshed once, post-setup, by `createWorkroom`.
68	      // Covers this window's create AND another window's, since `creatingWorkrooms` is shared.
69	      if isCreating(item.sid) { return false }
70	      // Nor one whose PROJECT has a commit in flight — see `isCommittingProject`. Also honoured on
71	      // `force`, because a manual Refresh during a long hook races the write just as readily as the
72	      // timer does.
73	      if isCommittingProject(item.projectRoot) { return false }
74	      guard !force else { return true }
75	      guard let checked = workroomStatuses[item.sid]?.lastChecked else { return true }
76	      return now.timeIntervalSince(checked) >= localTTL
77	    }
78	    // `.utility` so this background sweep yields CPU to a mounting terminal surface + its login shell.
79	    statusSweepTask = Task(priority: .utility) { [weak self] in
80	      guard let self else { return }
81	      await self.runLocalSweep(localItems, resolver: resolver, cap: Self.localConcurrency)
82	      if Task.isCancelled { return }
83	      // Guard the network stage: if `gh` isn't installed/authenticated, skip the whole CI sweep
84	      // rather than spawn a `gh` per dirty workroom only to have each fail.
85	      await self.refreshGitHubCLI(resolver: resolver, force: force)
86	      if Task.isCancelled { return }
87	      guard self.githubCLIStatus == .available else { return }
88	      let ciItems = self.statusWorkItems().filter { item in
89	        guard let s = self.workroomStatuses[item.sid], s.dirty != nil, s.failure == nil else {
90	          return false
91	        }
92	        guard !force else { return true }
93	        guard let c = s.ciCheckedAt else { return true }
94	        return now.timeIntervalSince(c) >= ciTTL
95	      }
96	      if Task.isCancelled { return }
97	      await self.runCISweep(ciItems, resolver: resolver, cap: Self.ciConcurrency)
98	    }
99	  }

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Which working-copy revision a `workingFileDiff` is against — backend-neutral so `DiffResolver`
4	/// maps its UI `DiffSource` onto it without knowing the backend:
5	///   - `.workingCopy` — the uncommitted changes: git = worktree/index vs `HEAD`; jj = `@` (vs `@-`).
6	///   - `.parent`      — jj only: the working copy's parent (`@-`) own changes (vs `@--`). Git has no
7	///     equivalent surface (git repos never request it) and reports it unsupported.
8	enum VCSWorkingDiffBase: Sendable, Equatable {
9	  case workingCopy
10	  case parent
11	}
12	
13	/// The single seam the app reads VCS data through. Two implementations — `RustJJProvider` (jj, over
14	/// the Rust/UniFFI core) and `GitProvider` (git, over SwiftGitX) — both return the app-native models
15	/// in `VCSModels.swift`. Views/models depend on this protocol, not on either backend.
16	protocol VCSProviding: Sendable {
17	  /// A bounded, newest-first page of history.
18	  ///
19	  /// "Newest-first" is deliberately each backend's OWN CLI order, not a shared one — the page is what
20	  /// `jj log` / `git log` would print, so History never contradicts the tool the user reaches for:
21	  /// jj is topological (children before parents, jj-lib's descending commit position), while git is
22	  /// reverse-chronological (libgit2's default `GIT_SORT_NONE`, matching git's date-ordered default

153	    // against a merge `@`'s auto-merged parents (a different base than the file list) and could be
154	    // read across an intervening edit. `VCSProviding` has no built-in timeout, so
155	    // bound the (synchronous, off-main) read with `withTimeout` — for `resolveGit` a wedged repo
156	    // abandons only its own caller. For THIS jj path that's no longer the full story: the read is
157	    // additionally serialized per project root through `gate` (the ONE jj read that mutates — takes
158	    // the working-copy lock, can commit a repo-level transaction — and a project's workrooms share
159	    // that repo-level store, so concurrent snapshots across them can contend; see `JJSnapshotGate`'s
160	    // doc). A genuinely wedged (never-returning) native call therefore doesn't just abandon its own
161	    // caller — it can block later same-project calls too, bounded by `JJSnapshotGate.maxChainWait`
162	    // (the gate self-heals past a hung predecessor instead of queuing behind it forever). `resolveGit`

164	    // unaffected.
165	    let root = URL(fileURLWithPath: dir, isDirectory: true)

### Git diff shows one side when a file is both staged and re-modified (macapp) — FIXED

**What:** `GitProvider` working diff/status use `entry.workingTree ?? entry.index`, so a file that is
staged AND further modified in the worktree renders only the working-tree (index→worktree) delta, not
the combined HEAD→worktree change.

**Fixed:** `workingFileDiff` now detects when a status entry carries BOTH an `.index` and a
`.workingTree` delta and, in that case, builds the diff from the file's HEAD blob (`nil` if it's new
since HEAD) to its current on-disk content (`GitProvider.combinedWorkingDiff`) — the same technique
`workingPatch`'s `.conflicted` case already used for a HEAD→worktree read. Covered by
`VCSProviderConformanceTests.testWorkingFileDiffCombinesStagedAndFurtherModifiedEdits` (staged-modify
+further-edit, and staged-add+further-edit).

**Priority:** done.

**Fixed:** `workingFileDiff` now detects when a status entry carries BOTH an `.index` and a
`.workingTree` delta and, in that case, builds the diff from the file's HEAD blob (`nil` if it's new
since HEAD) to its current on-disk content (`GitProvider.combinedWorkingDiff`) — the same technique
`workingPatch`'s `.conflicted` case already used for a HEAD→worktree read. Covered by
`VCSProviderConformanceTests.testWorkingFileDiffCombinesStagedAndFurtherModifiedEdits` (staged-modify
+further-edit, and staged-add+further-edit).

**Priority:** done.

### N-in-flight concurrency accounting test for status sweeps (macapp) — Muxy test-practices review follow-up — PARTIALLY FIXED

**What:** Add an injectable seam to `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit`/`resolveJJ` (they called
`GitProvider().workingStatus(root:)` and the native jj core directly, with no way to substitute a
double — `workingStatus` isn't on `VCSProviding`, so this was never `StatusCommandRunning`'s job),
then write a counting test on `runLocalSweep`'s `cap`-bounded `withTaskGroup` fan-out
(`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:457-529`) that asserts the number of concurrent local-status probes
never exceeds `cap`.

**Fixed, the `runLocalSweep` half:** `GitStatusReading`/`JJStatusReading` (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`)
are the new seams, injected via `WorkroomStatusResolver.init(gitStatus:jjStatus:)`, defaulting to the
real `GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider`. `WorkroomStatusConcurrencyTests.testLocalSweepNeverExceedsItsConcurrencyCap`
drives a real `AppStore` with 8 throwaway git projects and a counting `GitStatusReading` double,
asserting peak-concurrent calls stay ≤ 5 (`AppStore.localConcurrency`) and that the fan-out actually
overlapped (>1) — so the test can't pass vacuously against a fully serial sweep.

**Still open — the `runCISweep` half:** the CI stage's own cap (`ciConcurrency`, 2) has no equivalent
test. It fans out over `resolveCI`/`gh`, which already has an injectable `StatusCommandRunning` (see
`GatedGHRunner` in `WorkroomStatusTests.swift`) — the seam problem this entry was filed for doesn't
apply there, so it's a smaller remaining task: a counting `StatusCommandRunning` double + the same
shape of test against `runCISweep`.

**Priority:** P3 for the remainder — real gap, not urgent; no incident has surfaced it yet.

### `WindowDragUITests.testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips` is a known gesture-timing flake

**What:** Reproduced a pass then a fail on two consecutive back-to-back reruns of the identical test
against the identical binary during the beta.24 release gate — nothing else running, same machine,
same window geometry. Not caused by the beta.24 geometry fixes (fixture window 1200→1450pt): the
test computes its drag distance from the chips' own on-screen positions, so it's width-independent.

**Why:** The test's own comment already names the mechanism: "a slow drag with a hold at the end:
SwiftUI's reorder `DragGesture` needs the interpolated `onChanged` events and a settle before release
so `onEnded` commits (a fast one-shot drag can be missed)." `press(forDuration:thenDragTo:withVelocity:
thenHoldForDuration:)` synthesizes the interpolation itself, and how many intermediate events land
before the reorder's threshold check runs is not fully deterministic — occasionally too few land before
the drop, and `onEnded` sees the chip still under the threshold to swap.

**How to fix (not attempted — out of scope for the beta.24 gate, which needed to know this WASN'T a
regression, not eliminate it):** either add a manual multi-step drag (several discrete `press`+`moveTo`
calls before the final drop, giving the reorder logic more interpolated samples to react to) or lower
the reorder swap threshold's dependency on event count. Low priority: single test, single known flake
mode, not client-facing.

### `WindowDragUITests.testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips` is a known gesture-timing flake — IMPROVED, still flaky, still skipped

**What:** Reproduced a pass then a fail on two consecutive back-to-back reruns of the identical test
against the identical binary during the beta.24 release gate — nothing else running, same machine,
same window geometry. Not caused by the beta.24 geometry fixes (fixture window 1200→1450pt): the
test computes its drag distance from the chips' own on-screen positions, so it's width-independent.

**Real bug found and fixed along the way:** `WorkroomTabBar.commitDrag`/`TerminalTabStrip.commitDrag`
computed the reorder's drop index from the `dragTranslation` **state**, which is only ever written
inside `onChanged` — so a drag whose LAST `onChanged` sample landed short of the true release point
(any coarse/fast delivery, synthetic or real) commits off a stale, under-shot translation instead of
the gesture's own accurate final `value.translation` at `onEnded`. Fixed in both strips (they
deliberately mirror each other's reorder math) to read `value.translation` directly at commit time.
Correct regardless of whether it's THE cause of this flake — verified via the full `WindowDragUITests`
+ `WorkroomStatus*`/`VCSProviderConformanceTests` suites, no regressions.

**Measured, three iterations, ~30 back-to-back reruns total:**
1. The `commitDrag` fix alone: 1/5 passed. Ruled out as a full fix on its own.
2. + polling `chipsByX` until two reads agree (ruling out a race against the strip's own 0.2s
   reorder-settle `withAnimation`): 3/5.
3. + switching the gesture from the touch-oriented `press(forDuration:thenDragTo:…)` to the
   macOS-native mouse `click(forDuration:thenDragTo:…)` (same API family, `XCUICoordinateMouseEvents`,
   available on macOS): **9/10 in clean, uncontaminated batches** (one batch's first two runs were
   invalidated by an unrelated concurrent edit to `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift` mid-build — excluded).

**Still flaky — deliberately left skipped.** ~90% is a real improvement over the original coin-flip,
but not deterministic, and a ~1-in-10 spurious red X right before a release is its own cost. The
`APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip entry (`Makefile:67`) stays as-is.

**How to fix further (not attempted):** the TODO's original two ideas — a manual multi-step drag
giving the reorder logic more interpolated samples, or loosening the swap threshold's dependency on
event count — remain open, on top of whatever residual gap the native-mouse switch didn't close.
Low priority: single test, single known flake mode, not client-facing.

### Repo-level meta-test for Makefile/CI test invariants (macapp) — Muxy test-practices review follow-up

**What:** Add a check — in the existing dependency-free script tier alongside
`Scripts/build-helper_test.sh`/`Scripts/channel-helper_test.sh` (run via `make app-test-scripts`), not a
new XCTest class — that pins two invariants: the `APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list in `Makefile:67` (currently
4 tests: `AgentResumeUITests`, `SessionRestoreUITests`,
`HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive`,
`WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips`), and that release/nightly CI workflows
actually invoke `app-test` somewhere (not just that the Makefile's dependency graph excludes it from
`app-release`).

**Why:** These invariants live only in `Makefile` comments today. A refactor could silently drop a skip
entry (re-enabling a flaky/expensive UI test in the default local run) or silently remove the CI safety
net that runs `app-test` separately from `app-release` (since `app-release` deliberately does NOT depend
on it — Debug-only single-arch builds pin a different arch/signing shape than the release artifact).
Muxy has exactly this kind of guard (`TestIsolationScriptTests.swift`, reading its own `checks.sh` as
text and asserting it still invokes a test-isolation wrapper).

**Context:** Originally scoped as an XCTest class grepping `Makefile`/`ci.yml` strings; corrected during
outside-voice review — that couples the expensive, host-app-launching `WorkroomAppTests` bundle to
repository layout for what's really a spelling check, and the original CI-invariant framing (Makefile
dependency graph) checks the wrong thing. Pin the CI workflow's actual test invocations, not the Makefile
target graph. Full writeup at `~/.claude/plans/take-a-look-at-melodic-scott.md`.

**Depends on:** nothing.

**Priority:** P3 — real but low-urgency; nothing has drifted yet.

#!/bin/sh
#
# Dependency-free test for build-helper.sh's architecture handling. No bats/toolchain — just sh,
# go, and lipo. Run: sh macapp/Scripts/build-helper_test.sh   (exits non-zero on any mismatch).
#
# Why this exists: `ARCHS` is a SPACE-SEPARATED LIST, and build-helper.sh used to match it as a
# single token. A universal build hit the fallback and produced an arm64-only Go CLI inside a fat
# .app, with nothing louder than a `warn:` in the xcodebuild log. That shipped in every release from
# the app's first commit until it was caught by hand — on an Intel Mac the app launched and then
# failed at every workroom operation, since the app drives all of them through this binary.
#
# CI never catches it: `make app-test` builds Debug with a single native arch, so the multi-arch
# branch is only exercised by a real Release/Nightly build. Hence a standalone test.
set -u

DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# Overridable so the suite can be pointed at a modified copy — used to confirm these cases actually
# FAIL against the pre-fix single-token ARCHS logic rather than passing vacuously.
HELPER="${BUILD_HELPER:-${DIR}/build-helper.sh}"
fails=0

command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "build-helper_test: SKIP (go not on PATH)"; exit 0; }
command -v lipo >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "build-helper_test: SKIP (lipo not on PATH)"; exit 0; }

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# A throwaway Go module standing in for the repo root, so the test never depends on the real CLI
# building (or on its build time). build-helper.sh cds to $SRCROOT/.. to find the module.
mkdir -p "$WORK/module/macapp"
cat > "$WORK/module/go.mod" <<'EOF'
module buildhelpertest

go 1.21
EOF
cat > "$WORK/module/main.go" <<'EOF'
package main

var version = "dev"
var channel = ""

func main() {}
EOF

# run_helper <case-name> <ARCHS value> -> sets $OUT to the built helper path, $RC to the exit code
run_helper() {
  case_name="$1"
  archs="$2"
  dest="$WORK/out-$case_name"
  mkdir -p "$dest/Resources"
  OUT="$dest/Resources/workroom"
  SRCROOT="$WORK/module/macapp" \
  TARGET_BUILD_DIR="$dest" \
  UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH="Resources" \
  ARCHS="$archs" \
  MARKETING_VERSION="0.0.0-test" \
    sh "$HELPER" >"$dest/log" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

# expect_archs <case-name> <ARCHS value> <space-separated wanted archs>
expect_archs() {
  run_helper "$1" "$2"
  if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL: ARCHS='$2' exited $RC, want 0. Log:"
    sed 's/^/    /' "$WORK/out-$1/log"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
    return
  fi
  got="$(lipo -archs "$OUT" 2>/dev/null)"
  for want in $3; do
    case " $got " in
      *" $want "*) ;;
      *)
        echo "FAIL: ARCHS='$2' produced '$got', missing '$want'"
        fails=$((fails + 1))
        ;;
    esac
  done
  # No slice files may be left inside the bundle's Resources folder — they would be unsigned
  # binaries sealed into the shipped app.
  if ls "$(dirname "$OUT")"/workroom-slice-* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "FAIL: ARCHS='$2' left workroom-slice-* inside Resources"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# expect_failure <case-name> <ARCHS value> <substring the error must contain>
expect_failure() {
  run_helper "$1" "$2"
  if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL: ARCHS='$2' succeeded, want non-zero exit"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
    return
  fi
  if ! grep -q "$3" "$WORK/out-$1/log"; then
    echo "FAIL: ARCHS='$2' error did not mention '$3'. Log:"
    sed 's/^/    /' "$WORK/out-$1/log"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# The regression this file exists for: a universal build must produce BOTH slices.
expect_archs universal "arm64 x86_64" "arm64 x86_64"
# Order must not matter — Xcode does not promise one.
expect_archs reversed "x86_64 arm64" "arm64 x86_64"
# Single arch still works (the Debug path), and stays thin.
expect_archs solo_arm "arm64" "arm64"
expect_archs solo_intel "x86_64" "x86_64"
# An arch we cannot map is a hard error, not a silent arm64 fallback — that fallback IS the bug.

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-uitest. Skips the 3 most expensive/flaky cases by default (each
# does a real quit+relaunch or a hard timing budget), since XCUITest never runs in CI and a routine
# `make app-uitest` was paying ~4-5 min for tests that are only load-bearing right before a release.
# The isolation-tripwire tests those two classes carried (proving discovery/session-restore no-op
# without a seeded path — a guard the REST of this suite depends on) were extracted to
# `AgentSessionIsolationTripwireUITests` first, so the routine sweep keeps that safety net. Run the
# full suite (pre-release, or after touching any of these) with `make app-uitest APP_UITEST_FLAGS=`.
APP_UITEST_FLAGS ?= -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/SessionRestoreUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips

# The Rust VCS core (jj-lib via UniFFI) the app links, built into the local WrVcs SwiftPM package
# (vcs/swift/WrVcs). Must run before xcodegen so the package's xcframework + generated Swift exist.
# arm64 by default; release/distribution sets VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal (needs rustup stable >=
# 1.93 + both darwin targets, and `protoc` on PATH for jj-lib's build).
VCS_APPLE_FLAGS ?=
app-vcs: ## Build the Rust VCS core (xcframework + Swift bindings) the app links
	vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh $(VCS_APPLE_FLAGS)

app-run: app-build ## Build (Debug) and launch the dev app, replacing any running dev instance
	cd macapp || exit 1; \
	pkill -x "$(APP_NAME)" 2>/dev/null || true; \
	i=0; \
	while pgrep -x "$(APP_NAME)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ $$i -lt 40 ]; do \
	  sleep 0.2; i=$$((i + 1)); \
	done; \
	echo "Launching $(APP_BUNDLE)"; \
	open "$(APP_BUNDLE)"

app-build: app-vcs ## Build the app (Debug)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) build $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test: app-vcs ## Run the app's unit tests
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_TEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-uitest: app-vcs ## Run the app's UI tests (XCUITest — needs a real GUI login session, not headless)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_UITEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test-supervisor: ## Run the run-command supervisor PTY integration test (real shell + fake server)
	python3 macapp/Tests/run-supervisor/test_supervisor.py

app-test-scripts: ## Run the dependency-free shell-script tests (build-helper archs, channel classify)
	sh macapp/Scripts/build-helper_test.sh
	sh macapp/Scripts/channel-helper_test.sh

app-generate: app-vcs ## Force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate

app-format: ## Format Swift sources in place (swift-format)
	cd macapp && xcrun swift-format format --in-place --parallel --recursive WorkroomApp WorkroomAppTests WorkroomAppUITests

app-lint: ## Lint Swift with swift-format (--strict)
	cd macapp && xcrun swift-format lint --strict --parallel --recursive WorkroomApp WorkroomAppTests WorkroomAppUITests

app-release: VCS_APPLE_FLAGS := --universal
# `app-test-scripts` gates the release because it is the cheap half that catches an ARTIFACT bug
# (the universal-arch cases) and needs no toolchain, no keychain and no Xcode.
#
# `app-test` is deliberately NOT a prerequisite here. It builds Debug, and Debug pins
# `CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic` + `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: "Apple Development"` (project.yml). The
# release and nightly runners import a Developer ID certificate ONLY, and pass no APP_SIGN_FLAGS —
# so making it a prerequisite fails provisioning on a fresh runner before anything is archived.
# The xcodebuild suite runs as an explicit gate step in release.yml / nightly.yml instead, with the
# same ad-hoc overrides ci.yml uses.
app-release: app-vcs app-test-scripts ## Build, notarize, staple + package a DMG installer (macapp/Scripts/release.sh)
	cd macapp && Scripts/release.sh

app-icon: ## Regenerate release, dev + nightly AppIcon PNGs (macapp/Scripts/make-icon.swift)
	cd macapp && swift Scripts/make-icon.swift

app-clean: ## Remove the app's DerivedData + .xcodeproj
	cd macapp && rm -rf DerivedData $(APP_PROJECT)

#!/bin/sh
#
# Dependency-free meta-test pinning two test-infra invariants that otherwise live only in Makefile
# comments (Muxy test-practices review, filed in TODOS.md): the `APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list, and
# that release/nightly/CI workflows still actually invoke `make app-test` somewhere. No toolchain —
# just sh + grep. Run: sh macapp/Scripts/test-invariants_test.sh   (exits non-zero on any mismatch).
#
# Why a shell script and not an XCTest class: an XCTest class would couple the expensive,
# host-app-launching WorkroomAppTests bundle to repository layout for what's really a spelling
# check, and reading the Makefile's dependency GRAPH (does app-release depend on app-test?) checks
# the wrong thing — app-release deliberately does NOT depend on app-test (Debug-only single-arch
# builds pin a different signing shape than the release artifact; see the Makefile's app-release
# comment). The real invariant lives in the CI workflows that run the xcodebuild suite as an
# explicit step instead.
set -u

DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$DIR/../.." && pwd)"
MAKEFILE="$ROOT/Makefile"
fails=0

# --- APP_UITEST_FLAGS skip list -------------------------------------------------------------
# Pinned literally: a refactor that silently drops or adds an entry re-enables (or newly skips) a
# flaky/expensive UI test in the default local `make app-uitest` run without anyone deciding to.
want_flags='-skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/SessionRestoreUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips'
got_flags="$(sed -n 's/^APP_UITEST_FLAGS ?= //p' "$MAKEFILE")"
if [ "$got_flags" != "$want_flags" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: Makefile's APP_UITEST_FLAGS skip list changed."
  echo "  want: $want_flags"
  echo "  got:  $got_flags"
  fails=$((fails + 1))
fi

# --- app-test still wired into CI ------------------------------------------------------------
# Pin the workflows' actual invocation of the xcodebuild suite, not the Makefile's dependency
# graph (which deliberately excludes app-test from app-release). `([^-]|$)` excludes
# `app-test-scripts`/`app-test-supervisor`, which are different targets entirely.
for wf in ci.yml release.yml nightly.yml; do
  path="$ROOT/.github/workflows/$wf"
  if [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: workflow $wf not found at $path"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
    continue
  fi
  if ! grep -Eq 'make app-test([^-]|$)' "$path"; then
    echo "FAIL: $wf no longer invokes 'make app-test' — the unit-test safety net may be gone"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
done

if [ "$fails" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "test-invariants_test: $fails failure(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "test-invariants_test: all cases passed"

#!/bin/sh
#
# Dependency-free meta-test pinning two test-infra invariants that otherwise live only in Makefile
# comments (Muxy test-practices review, filed in TODOS.md): the `APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list, and
# that release/nightly/CI workflows still actually invoke `make app-test` somewhere. No toolchain —
# just sh + grep. Run: sh macapp/Scripts/test-invariants_test.sh   (exits non-zero on any mismatch).
#
# Why a shell script and not an XCTest class: an XCTest class would couple the expensive,
# host-app-launching WorkroomAppTests bundle to repository layout for what's really a spelling
# check, and reading the Makefile's dependency GRAPH (does app-release depend on app-test?) checks
# the wrong thing — app-release deliberately does NOT depend on app-test (Debug-only single-arch
# builds pin a different signing shape than the release artifact; see the Makefile's app-release
# comment). The real invariant lives in the CI workflows that run the xcodebuild suite as an
# explicit step instead.
set -u

DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$DIR/../.." && pwd)"
MAKEFILE="$ROOT/Makefile"
fails=0

# --- APP_UITEST_FLAGS skip list -------------------------------------------------------------
# Pinned literally: a refactor that silently drops or adds an entry re-enables (or newly skips) a
# flaky/expensive UI test in the default local `make app-uitest` run without anyone deciding to.
want_flags='-skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/SessionRestoreUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips'
got_flags="$(sed -n 's/^APP_UITEST_FLAGS ?= //p' "$MAKEFILE")"
if [ "$got_flags" != "$want_flags" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: Makefile's APP_UITEST_FLAGS skip list changed."
  echo "  want: $want_flags"
  echo "  got:  $got_flags"
  fails=$((fails + 1))
fi

# --- app-test still wired into CI ------------------------------------------------------------
# Pin the workflows' actual invocation of the xcodebuild suite, not the Makefile's dependency
# graph (which deliberately excludes app-test from app-release). `([^-]|$)` excludes
# `app-test-scripts`/`app-test-supervisor`, which are different targets entirely.
for wf in ci.yml release.yml nightly.yml; do
  path="$ROOT/.github/workflows/$wf"
  if [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: workflow $wf not found at $path"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
    continue
  fi
  if ! grep -Eq 'make app-test([^-]|$)' "$path"; then
    echo "FAIL: $wf no longer invokes 'make app-test' — the unit-test safety net may be gone"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
done

if [ "$fails" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "test-invariants_test: $fails failure(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "test-invariants_test: all cases passed"

# Repo-wide dev tasks, namespaced: `cli-*` = the Go CLI (the primary product), `app-*` = the
# macOS app under macapp/ (Xcode-based). Run `make` with no target to list them.
#
# App recipes run inside macapp/ and need its toolchain on PATH (xcodegen via Homebrew). The
# Xcode build also runs project.yml phases — a non-fatal swift-format lint and embedding the Go
# helper (macapp/Scripts/build-helper.sh). `cli-lint` needs golangci-lint installed (see CLAUDE.md).
export PATH := /opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$(PATH)
VERSION ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help
.PHONY: help \
        cli-build cli-test cli-install cli-lint cli-clean \
        app-vcs app-run app-build app-test app-uitest app-test-supervisor app-test-scripts app-generate app-format app-lint app-release app-icon app-clean

help: ## List available targets
	@grep -hE '^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) \
	  | awk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*## "}{printf "  \033[36m%-13s\033[0m %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

# --- Go CLI (repo root) ---

cli-build: ## Build the workroom binary (version injected)
	go build -ldflags "-X main.version=$(VERSION)" -o workroom .

cli-test: ## Run the Go tests
	go test ./...

cli-install: ## Install the binary to $GOBIN
	go install -ldflags "-X main.version=$(VERSION)" .

cli-lint: ## Lint Go with golangci-lint
	golangci-lint run

cli-clean: ## Remove the built binary
	rm -f workroom

# --- macOS app (macapp/) ---

# The Debug product is "Workroom Dev" (distinct bundle id + name) so it runs alongside the
# installed release "Workroom" without conflict — see macapp/project.yml.
APP_PROJECT := WorkroomApp.xcodeproj
APP_NAME    := Workroom Dev
APP_BUNDLE  := DerivedData/Build/Products/Debug/$(APP_NAME).app
APP_XCODEBUILD := xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomApp -configuration Debug \
  -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages

# Extra xcodebuild build-setting overrides, appended to app-build/app-test. Empty locally so
# ⌘R-style automatic signing is used; CI sets this to ad-hoc / no-team signing because hosted
# runners have no signing cert or DEVELOPMENT_TEAM (e.g.
# `make app-test APP_SIGN_FLAGS="CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="`).
APP_SIGN_FLAGS ?=

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-test. Parallel execution by default: the suite is dominated by a
# few slow integration classes (Markdown WebView renders, real git/jj repos), so spreading classes
# across worker processes cuts the run ~40% (48s -> ~29s). Each worker gets its own host-app process
# but they share one UserDefaults domain, so a test mutating a `Defaults` key another class reads
# would race — override with `make app-test APP_TEST_FLAGS=` to bisect a suspected parallel-only
# failure. Test dirs are already UUID-scoped under NSTemporaryDirectory, so those don't collide.
APP_TEST_FLAGS ?= -parallel-testing-enabled YES

# Extra xcodebuild options for app-uitest. Skips the 3 most expensive/flaky cases by default (each
# does a real quit+relaunch or a hard timing budget), since XCUITest never runs in CI and a routine
# `make app-uitest` was paying ~4-5 min for tests that are only load-bearing right before a release.
# The isolation-tripwire tests those two classes carried (proving discovery/session-restore no-op
# without a seeded path — a guard the REST of this suite depends on) were extracted to
# `AgentSessionIsolationTripwireUITests` first, so the routine sweep keeps that safety net. Run the
# full suite (pre-release, or after touching any of these) with `make app-uitest APP_UITEST_FLAGS=`.
APP_UITEST_FLAGS ?= -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/SessionRestoreUITests -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive -skip-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips

# The Rust VCS core (jj-lib via UniFFI) the app links, built into the local WrVcs SwiftPM package
# (vcs/swift/WrVcs). Must run before xcodegen so the package's xcframework + generated Swift exist.
# arm64 by default; release/distribution sets VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal (needs rustup stable >=
# 1.93 + both darwin targets, and `protoc` on PATH for jj-lib's build).
VCS_APPLE_FLAGS ?=
app-vcs: ## Build the Rust VCS core (xcframework + Swift bindings) the app links
	vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh $(VCS_APPLE_FLAGS)

app-run: app-build ## Build (Debug) and launch the dev app, replacing any running dev instance
	cd macapp || exit 1; \
	pkill -x "$(APP_NAME)" 2>/dev/null || true; \
	i=0; \
	while pgrep -x "$(APP_NAME)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ $$i -lt 40 ]; do \
	  sleep 0.2; i=$$((i + 1)); \
	done; \
	echo "Launching $(APP_BUNDLE)"; \
	open "$(APP_BUNDLE)"

app-build: app-vcs ## Build the app (Debug)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) build $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test: app-vcs ## Run the app's unit tests
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && $(APP_XCODEBUILD) -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_TEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-uitest: app-vcs ## Run the app's UI tests (XCUITest — needs a real GUI login session, not headless)
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project $(APP_PROJECT) -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' $(APP_UITEST_FLAGS) test $(APP_SIGN_FLAGS)

app-test-supervisor: ## Run the run-command supervisor PTY integration test (real shell + fake server)
	python3 macapp/Tests/run-supervisor/test_supervisor.py

app-test-scripts: ## Run the dependency-free shell-script tests (build-helper archs, channel classify)
	sh macapp/Scripts/build-helper_test.sh
	sh macapp/Scripts/channel-helper_test.sh

app-generate: app-vcs ## Force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
	cd macapp && xcodegen generate

app-format: ## Format Swift sources in place (swift-format)
	cd macapp && xcrun swift-format format --in-place --parallel --recursive WorkroomApp WorkroomAppTests WorkroomAppUITests

app-lint: ## Lint Swift with swift-format (--strict)
	cd macapp && xcrun swift-format lint --strict --parallel --recursive WorkroomApp WorkroomAppTests WorkroomAppUITests

app-release: VCS_APPLE_FLAGS := --universal
# `app-test-scripts` gates the release because it is the cheap half that catches an ARTIFACT bug
# (the universal-arch cases) and needs no toolchain, no keychain and no Xcode.
#
# `app-test` is deliberately NOT a prerequisite here. It builds Debug, and Debug pins
# `CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic` + `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: "Apple Development"` (project.yml). The
# release and nightly runners import a Developer ID certificate ONLY, and pass no APP_SIGN_FLAGS —
# so making it a prerequisite fails provisioning on a fresh runner before anything is archived.
# The xcodebuild suite runs as an explicit gate step in release.yml / nightly.yml instead, with the
# same ad-hoc overrides ci.yml uses.
app-release: app-vcs app-test-scripts ## Build, notarize, staple + package a DMG installer (macapp/Scripts/release.sh)
	cd macapp && Scripts/release.sh

app-icon: ## Regenerate release, dev + nightly AppIcon PNGs (macapp/Scripts/make-icon.swift)
	cd macapp && swift Scripts/make-icon.swift

app-clean: ## Remove the app's DerivedData + .xcodeproj
	cd macapp && rm -rf DerivedData $(APP_PROJECT)

### Repo-level meta-test for Makefile/CI test invariants (macapp) — Muxy test-practices review follow-up

**What:** Add a check — in the existing dependency-free script tier alongside
`Scripts/build-helper_test.sh`/`Scripts/channel-helper_test.sh` (run via `make app-test-scripts`), not a
new XCTest class — that pins two invariants: the `APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list in `Makefile:67` (currently
4 tests: `AgentResumeUITests`, `SessionRestoreUITests`,
`HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive`,
`WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips`), and that release/nightly CI workflows
actually invoke `app-test` somewhere (not just that the Makefile's dependency graph excludes it from
`app-release`).

**Why:** These invariants live only in `Makefile` comments today. A refactor could silently drop a skip
entry (re-enabling a flaky/expensive UI test in the default local run) or silently remove the CI safety
net that runs `app-test` separately from `app-release` (since `app-release` deliberately does NOT depend
on it — Debug-only single-arch builds pin a different arch/signing shape than the release artifact).
Muxy has exactly this kind of guard (`TestIsolationScriptTests.swift`, reading its own `checks.sh` as
text and asserting it still invokes a test-isolation wrapper).

**Context:** Originally scoped as an XCTest class grepping `Makefile`/`ci.yml` strings; corrected during
outside-voice review — that couples the expensive, host-app-launching `WorkroomAppTests` bundle to
repository layout for what's really a spelling check, and the original CI-invariant framing (Makefile
dependency graph) checks the wrong thing. Pin the CI workflow's actual test invocations, not the Makefile
target graph. Full writeup at `~/.claude/plans/take-a-look-at-melodic-scott.md`.

**Depends on:** nothing.

**Priority:** P3 — real but low-urgency; nothing has drifted yet.
