1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Thrown by `withTimeout` when the operation outruns its deadline.
4	struct VCSTimeoutError: Error {}
5	
6	/// Run `operation`, throwing `VCSTimeoutError` if it doesn't finish within `seconds`. On timeout the
7	/// operation task is cancelled and its eventual result dropped.
8	///
9	/// This is the timeout seam the VCS resolvers (`BranchResolver`, `WorkroomStatusResolver`) rely on
10	/// now that their reads go through `VCSProviding` — which, unlike the old CLI command-runners, has
11	/// no built-in per-call timeout/kill. Caveat: an in-flight *synchronous* backend read (libgit2 /
12	/// jj-lib over UniFFI) can't be interrupted mid-call, so on timeout it keeps running to completion
13	/// on its own thread and its result is abandoned. That still delivers the resolvers' contract — one
14	/// wedged repo abandons only its own row and never blocks the others.
15	///
16	/// Implemented as a first-to-settle race over a single continuation, NOT a `withThrowingTaskGroup`:
17	/// a task group awaits ALL its children before returning, so when the deadline child wins the group
18	/// would still block on the (uncancellable, synchronous) operation child until it finished —
19	/// silently defeating the timeout for exactly the wedged-read case it exists to bound. The
20	/// continuation resumes the caller the instant either side settles.
21	func withTimeout<T: Sendable>(
22	  seconds: TimeInterval, _ operation: @escaping @Sendable () async throws -> T
23	) async throws -> T {
24	  try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { (cont: CheckedContinuation<T, Error>) in
25	    let gate = TimeoutGate(cont)
26	    let op = Task {
27	      do { gate.settle(.success(try await operation())) } catch { gate.settle(.failure(error)) }
28	    }
29	    Task {
30	      try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(max(0, seconds) * 1_000_000_000))
31	      gate.settle(.failure(VCSTimeoutError()))
32	      // Best-effort: abandons the loser (uncancellable native work runs on to no effect).
33	      op.cancel()
34	    }
35	  }
36	}
37	
38	/// Resumes a `withTimeout` continuation exactly once — the operation-completes vs deadline-fires race.
39	private final class TimeoutGate<T: Sendable>: @unchecked Sendable {
40	  private let lock = NSLock()
41	  private var done = false
42	  private let cont: CheckedContinuation<T, Error>
43	  init(_ cont: CheckedContinuation<T, Error>) { self.cont = cont }
44	  func settle(_ result: Result<T, Error>) {
45	    lock.lock()
46	    let first = !done
47	    done = true
48	    lock.unlock()
49	    if first { cont.resume(with: result) }
50	  }
51	}
52	
53	/// Run a synchronous, blocking closure OFF the Swift cooperative thread pool — on GCD's global queue,
54	/// whose threads grow on demand.
55	///
56	/// The VCS backends' reads (jj-lib over UniFFI, libgit2) block their thread for the whole call. Run
57	/// on the cooperative pool (`Task.detached`), a burst of them — e.g. the per-workroom status
58	/// snapshots fanned out on selection (`refreshWorkroomStatuses`' task group) — saturates its fixed
59	/// width (≈ core count) and starves any other blocking read queued behind it. That's the "History
60	/// pane loads forever" bug: its read waited behind the status burst until the pool drained (a tab
61	/// switch just bought it time). GCD hands each read a thread immediately, so they don't starve.
62	///
63	/// Like `withTimeout`'s detached read, the call can't be cancelled mid-flight; a cancelled caller
64	/// just abandons the result once the closure returns.
65	func runBlocking<T: Sendable>(
66	  qos: DispatchQoS.QoSClass = .userInitiated, _ work: @escaping @Sendable () throws -> T
67	) async throws -> T {
68	  try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
69	    DispatchQueue.global(qos: qos).async {
70	      continuation.resume(with: Result(catching: work))
71	    }
72	  }
73	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Serializes jj working-copy snapshots per project root (VCS-foundation eng-review). A jj
4	/// `working_status`/`workingFileDiff(.workingCopy)` call *snapshots* `@` — it takes the
5	/// per-workspace working-copy lock and, if the tree changed, commits a **repo-level** transaction
6	/// against the shared op-store. All of a project's workrooms (secondary jj workspaces) fund into
7	/// that same repo-level store, and git worktrees of one project share the backing `.git`, so
8	/// concurrent snapshots across a project's workrooms can contend (observed live as a
9	/// `packed-refs.lock could not be obtained` error) even though each workspace's own lock is never
10	/// itself shared cross-workroom.
11	///
12	/// A single global gate would needlessly serialize unrelated projects against each other, so this
13	/// keys per project root: a chain-of-tails per key, implemented as a plain `actor` (no `NSLock`/
14	/// `DispatchQueue` — mirrors the `DiffCache` actor already in this codebase for a similar
15	/// cross-call-site coordination need). `tails` is never evicted — bounded by the number of
16	/// distinct project roots swept in a process lifetime, not by call volume.
17	///
18	/// **Callers must pass the raw, untimed native call as `operation`.** `withTimeout` (see
19	/// `Timeout.swift`) can't truly cancel a synchronous jj-lib call — it only abandons *waiting* on
20	/// it, and the call keeps running to completion on its own thread underneath. If a timeout wrapped
21	/// the operation *inside* the gate, the gate would treat the call as "done" the instant it's
22	/// abandoned, letting the next queued call start snapshotting while the abandoned one still
23	/// physically holds the lock — reproducing the exact race this gate exists to close. So the
24	/// correct composition is always `withTimeout(seconds:) { gate.run(projectRoot:) { rawCall() } }`
25	/// — the timeout wraps the *wait*, the gate wraps the *ordering*, the native call is innermost and
26	/// un-timed.
27	///
28	/// **A genuinely-hung (never-returning) native call is bounded, not fatal to the queue.** Because a
29	/// predecessor's call can't be cancelled (above), naively `await`-ing it forever would mean a truly
30	/// wedged jj-lib call (jj CLI pipe deadlocks have happened before in this codebase's history)
31	/// permanently blocks every future same-project call — worse than the pre-gate world, where each
32	/// lane's own independent timeout at least bounded ITS OWN wait. `maxChainWait` fixes this: a new
33	/// call waits for its predecessor only up to that ceiling, then gives up waiting and runs its own
34	/// operation anyway. The abandoned predecessor keeps running harmlessly in the background (nothing
35	/// awaits it once given up on); the chain self-heals within one ceiling's worth of delay instead of
36	/// wedging forever. The cost: giving up on a predecessor early re-admits the ORIGINAL race (two
37	/// operations physically overlapping) for that one occurrence — but only in the rare genuine-wedge
38	/// case, not for routine (fast, bounded) contention, which `maxChainWait` is sized well above.
39	actor JJSnapshotGate {
40	  /// The process-wide gate. Must be process-global, not an `AppStore` property — `AppStore` is
41	  /// instantiated fresh per window (`WorkroomApp.swift`), so a gate stored there would serialize
42	  /// nothing across windows even though multiple windows commonly sweep the same projects.
43	  static let shared = JJSnapshotGate()
44	
45	  /// Default for `maxChainWait` — how long a new call waits for a same-project predecessor before
46	  /// giving up on it and running anyway (see the type doc's "genuinely-hung" section). Deliberately
47	  /// much larger than `WorkroomStatusResolver.jjGatedWaitTimeout` (15s, the caller-facing per-call
48	  /// budget) — a single healthy jj snapshot normally finishes in well under a second, so this should
49	  /// only ever be hit by a genuine wedge, never by routine same-project queuing.
50	  static let defaultMaxChainWait: TimeInterval = 30
51	
52	  private let maxChainWait: TimeInterval
53	  /// The most recently scheduled call's completion, per project root — the tail of that project's
54	  /// chain. A new call waits for this before running, then becomes the new tail.
55	  private var tails: [String: Task<Void, Never>] = [:]
56	
57	  /// Non-private so tests construct an isolated gate instead of sharing the process-wide singleton.
58	  /// `maxChainWait` is injectable (default `defaultMaxChainWait`) so a test can use a short ceiling
59	  /// to exercise self-healing without a real 30s wait — mirrors `DiffCache(budget:)`.
60	  init(maxChainWait: TimeInterval = JJSnapshotGate.defaultMaxChainWait) {
61	    self.maxChainWait = maxChainWait
62	  }
63	
64	  /// Run `operation` after any earlier same-`projectRoot` call has genuinely finished, OR after
65	  /// `maxChainWait` elapses waiting on it (self-healing — see the type doc). Calls for different
66	  /// project roots never wait on each other. A call cancelled before its turn arrives never invokes
67	  /// `operation`. `operation` must never itself call `run(projectRoot:)` for the SAME `projectRoot`
68	  /// (directly or transitively) — that would wait on its own tail and deadlock that project's queue
69	  /// for up to `maxChainWait`. No current caller does this; it's a caller invariant, not something
70	  /// this type can detect or guard against.
71	  func run<T: Sendable>(
72	    projectRoot: String, _ operation: @Sendable @escaping () async throws -> T
73	  ) async throws -> T {
74	    let previous = tails[projectRoot]
75	    let task = Task<T, Error> {
76	      if let previous {
77	        // `withTimeout`, not a task group: a task group awaits all children before returning, so a
78	        // still-wedged `previous` would block this wait past its own ceiling — exactly the trap
79	        // `Timeout.swift`'s own doc warns about. `withTimeout` races via a continuation instead, so
80	        // it actually returns at the ceiling regardless of whether `previous` has finished.
81	        _ = try? await withTimeout(seconds: maxChainWait) { await previous.value }
82	      }
83	      try Task.checkCancellation()
84	      return try await operation()
85	    }
86	    tails[projectRoot] = Task<Void, Never> { _ = try? await task.value }
87	    return try await withTaskCancellationHandler {
88	      try await task.value
89	    } onCancel: {
90	      task.cancel()
91	    }
92	  }
93	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Resolves a project root's current branch/bookmark for the sidebar root-row label — the `@`
4	/// bookmark / nearest ancestor bookmark (jj) or current branch / short SHA (git) — read structurally
5	/// through `VCSProviding` (jj via jj-lib, git via SwiftGitX). GUI-only: the `workroom` CLI never
6	/// shows it, and resolving per project (not inside `list --json`) keeps the list instant and
7	/// isolates a slow/wedged repo to its own row. Best-effort — any failure or timeout yields
8	/// `.unresolved` for that project and never affects others.
9	///
10	/// (Previously shelled `git symbolic-ref` / `jj log -T bookmarks` and parsed the output; the jj
11	/// bookmark cleaning + nearest-ancestor walk now live in the Rust core's `current_ref`, and jj-lib's
12	/// `local_bookmarks()` yields clean names — no `*`/`?`/`@` decoration to strip. The read stays
13	/// lock-safe: `current_ref` never snapshots the working copy, so it can't self-trigger the
14	/// `.jj` file watcher.)
15	struct BranchResolver: Sendable {
16	  /// Per-call ceiling so one hung repo abandons only its own label. `VCSProviding` has no built-in
17	  /// timeout, so this wraps the read in `withTimeout`.
18	  var timeout: TimeInterval
19	  /// The VCS backend, injected for tests. Defaults to the real repo-kind router.
20	  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
21	
22	  init(
23	    timeout: TimeInterval = 3,
24	    makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) }
25	  ) {
26	    self.timeout = timeout
27	    self.makeProvider = makeProvider
28	  }
29	
30	  func resolve(path: String, vcs: String) async -> RootRef {
31	    // Only git/jj projects have a resolvable root ref; anything else has no label. (The provider
32	    // itself routes jj vs git by repo kind — this guard just skips the unsupported case.)
33	    guard vcs == "git" || vcs == "jj" else { return .unresolved }
34	    let root = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true)
35	    do {
36	      let ref = try await withTimeout(seconds: timeout) {
37	        // The provider self-offloads its blocking read to GCD (`runBlocking`), so a plain await here
38	        // never occupies a cooperative-pool thread — no `Task.detached` wrapper needed.
39	        try await makeProvider(root).currentRef(root: root)
40	      }
41	      return Self.rootRef(from: ref)
42	    } catch {
43	      return .unresolved
44	    }
45	  }
46

48	  /// `.unresolved`, so an unlabelled repo never clobbers a prior label (the caller keeps the old
49	  /// value on `.unresolved`). `branch` is normalized to nil-never-"" per `RootRef`'s contract.

605	### `withTimeout` doesn't observe the CALLER's own cancellation (macapp) — VCS-foundation eng-review, /review follow-up
606	
607	**Status:** the original version of this entry (a `withThrowingTaskGroup` awaiting a detached
608	operation child past its own deadline) is **fixed** — `Core/Timeout.swift` now races via a single
609	`withCheckedThrowingContinuation` + a `TimeoutGate`, exactly the fix this entry used to recommend.
610	Re-audited during the jj-snapshot-serialization `/review` (2026-07-24, cross-model: Codex found it)
611	and found a **different, still-live** gap in that same seam.
612	
613	**What:** `withTimeout`'s `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` only resolves on ITS OWN internal race
614	(the operation finishing vs. its own `seconds` deadline firing) — it never wires up
615	`withTaskCancellationHandler`, so it does not observe the CALLING task being cancelled from outside.
616	Concretely: `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`'s `statusSweepTask?.cancel()` (a new sweep replacing an
617	old one) propagates into `runLocalSweep`'s `withTaskGroup` children structurally, but a cancelled
618	child's in-flight `withTimeout(seconds:) { … }` call (inside `resolveJJ`/`resolveGit`) keeps running
619	to completion (or its own `seconds` timeout) regardless — it doesn't stop early just because the
620	enclosing task gave up.
621	
622	**Why:** Wastes CPU/time re-running a probe nobody wants anymore, and — post the jj-snapshot-gate
623	fix — adds unnecessary extra contention pressure on `JJSnapshotGate` (an unwanted, already-abandoned
624	caller still occupies a project's queue slot for up to its full timeout). This is a
625	responsiveness/efficiency gap, not a data-integrity one, because the call sites in this seam do
626	check `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result (`runLocalSweep`'s
627	`if Task.isCancelled { break }`, etc.).
628	
629	**Corrected 2026-08-05 — do NOT re-read this entry as "the convention protects us".** This used to
630	say *every* call site already checks, so state stays correct. That was false, and the counterexample
631	shipped: `refreshGitHubCLI` mutated `githubCLIStatus` **inside** an awaited function, where the
632	callers' own guards (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:86`/`:144`) run too late to help. A cancelled
633	probe's SIGKILLed `gh` still returned through `StatusCommandRunner`'s non-throwing continuation with
634	the signal number as its exit code, the classifier read that as "not signed in", and publishing it
635	*stamped the TTL* — so the wrong value suppressed its own repair for a full minute. The cost of a
636	missed guard is therefore a **wrong published value**, not merely a wasted probe. Two defences
637	landed with that fix and are what keeps the residual risk low: `CommandResult.signaled` (a killed
638	child is never mistaken for a CLI that ran and failed) and `GHAuthProbe.keepPrior` (a non-answer
639	neither writes nor stamps). The `withTimeout` gap below is a genuinely different mechanism and stays
640	deferred on its own merits.
641	
642	**How to start:** Wrap `withTimeout`'s continuation in `withTaskCancellationHandler` so cancelling
643	the calling task settles the `TimeoutGate` early (same shape `JJSnapshotGate.run` already uses to
644	propagate cancellation into its own chained `Task`). Verify the existing "operation keeps running,
645	result dropped" contract still holds — this only makes the WAIT responsive to cancellation, not the
646	underlying synchronous native call (still uncancellable, unchanged).
647	
648	**Depends on:** —. Touches `Core/Timeout.swift`. Broad blast radius (every `withTimeout` caller:
649	`WorkroomStatusResolver`, `BranchResolver`, `JJSnapshotGate`'s own internal use) — needs its own
650	careful review/testing, not a drive-by fix.
651	
652	**Priority:** P2 (efficiency/responsiveness, not correctness; no user-visible bug today).

Re-audited during the jj-snapshot-serialization `/review` (2026-07-24, cross-model: Codex found it)
and found a **different, still-live** gap in that same seam.

**What:** `withTimeout`'s `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` only resolves on ITS OWN internal race
(the operation finishing vs. its own `seconds` deadline firing) — it never wires up
`withTaskCancellationHandler`, so it does not observe the CALLING task being cancelled from outside.
Concretely: `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`'s `statusSweepTask?.cancel()` (a new sweep replacing an
old one) propagates into `runLocalSweep`'s `withTaskGroup` children structurally, but a cancelled
child's in-flight `withTimeout(seconds:) { … }` call (inside `resolveJJ`/`resolveGit`) keeps running
to completion (or its own `seconds` timeout) regardless — it doesn't stop early just because the
enclosing task gave up.

**Why:** Wastes CPU/time re-running a probe nobody wants anymore, and — post the jj-snapshot-gate
fix — adds unnecessary extra contention pressure on `JJSnapshotGate` (an unwanted, already-abandoned
caller still occupies a project's queue slot for up to its full timeout). This is a
responsiveness/efficiency gap, not a data-integrity one, because the call sites in this seam do
check `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result (`runLocalSweep`'s
`if Task.isCancelled { break }`, etc.).

**Corrected 2026-08-05 — do NOT re-read this entry as "the convention protects us".** This used to
say *every* call site already checks, so state stays correct. That was false, and the counterexample
shipped: `refreshGitHubCLI` mutated `githubCLIStatus` **inside** an awaited function, where the
callers' own guards (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:86`/`:144`) run too late to help. A cancelled

missed guard is therefore a **wrong published value**, not merely a wasted probe. Two defences

deferred on its own merits.

the calling task settles the `TimeoutGate` early (same shape `JJSnapshotGate.run` already uses to

### `withTimeout` doesn't observe the CALLER's own cancellation (macapp) — FIXED

**Status:** the original version of this entry (a `withThrowingTaskGroup` awaiting a detached
operation child past its own deadline) is **fixed** — `Core/Timeout.swift` now races via a single
`withCheckedThrowingContinuation` + a `TimeoutGate`, exactly the fix this entry used to recommend.
Re-audited during the jj-snapshot-serialization `/review` (2026-07-24, cross-model: Codex found it)
and found a **different, still-live** gap in that same seam — **now also fixed.**

**Fixed:** `withTimeout` wraps its continuation in `withTaskCancellationHandler` (a `TimeoutCancelBox`
bridges `onCancel`, which Swift can invoke before/during/after the continuation attaches, to settling
the SAME `TimeoutGate` early with a new `VCSCancellationError`) — same shape `JJSnapshotGate.run`
already used. `WorkroomStatusResolver`'s two catch sites treat `VCSCancellationError` the same as
`VCSTimeoutError`; `BranchResolver`'s blanket `catch` and `JJSnapshotGate`'s own `try?` call were
already safe either way. `TimeoutTests.swift` (previously zero coverage on this seam) covers the
success/deadline baselines plus both cancellation orderings (mid-race and already-cancelled-at-call)
and a 200-iteration stress test for the exactly-once settle guarantee; the cancellation test itself
proves the fix by needing well under 1s against a 5s deadline/operation, not the full wait. Full
`WorkroomStatusResolverTests`/`WorkroomStatusConcurrencyTests`/`BranchResolverTests`/
`VCSProviderConformanceTests` sweep green, no regressions.

---
name: macapp-full-parallel-suite-flake
description: "make app-test (full ~2270-test parallel suite) intermittently fails 1-3 unrelated timing-sensitive tests per run, a DIFFERENT random subset each time — not a regression, don't chase it per-commit."
metadata:
  type: project
---

`make app-test` run 3x back-to-back on 2026-08-13 (after a long session of heavy concurrent
xcodebuild/XCUITest activity) failed with 2, then 1, then 3 failing tests — **zero overlap** across
the three runs (5 distinct tests total: `AppStoreCreateWorkroomTests.testWorktreeProbedOnceCreatingClears`,
`RunCommandTests.testRequestCloseWaitsForLiveRunCommand`, `AppStoreCreateWorkroomTests.testCreationTargetAppearsAsTab`,
`SessionSaveTests.testAFailedWriteIsNotRememberedAsWritten`, `RunCommandTests.testSecondStopWaitsForLiveProcessThenCloses`,
`AppStoreDeleteRaceTests.testDeleteBlockedWhileCreating`).

Two of them (`testWorktreeProbedOnceCreatingClears`, `testRequestCloseWaitsForLiveRunCommand`)
re-ran clean 4/4 in isolation (`-only-testing` scoped to just those two, not the full parallel
suite). The rotating, non-overlapping failure set + clean isolated reruns point to **CPU-contention
flakiness under `-parallel-testing-enabled` on a loaded machine**, not a deterministic logic bug —
several of these tests use fixed wall-clock sleep budgets (e.g. 500ms) waiting for async work that
can occasionally lose the race under load, and none share a code path with each other.

**How to apply:** a single red `make app-test` (whole-suite, parallel) run is NOT strong evidence of
a real regression on its own — rerun the SPECIFIC failing test(s) with `-only-testing` before
concluding a change broke something. If the same test fails deterministically in isolation, that's
real; if it passes in isolation, treat the full-suite run as noise from machine load. Related:
[[macapp-xcuitest-automation-wedge]] (same "environmental, not code" pattern for XCUITest launches).

115	      // empties the store, so the list drops to its "No notifications" state (the popover stays open).

content.subject: Fix withTimeout not observing caller's own cancellation
content.description: TODOS.md line 608. Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. Wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancelling the caller settles TimeoutGate early (same shape as JJSnapshotGate.run). Broad blast radius (WorkroomStatusResolver, BranchResolver, JJSnapshotGate's own use) - needs task #7's test harness in place first to verify the fix observably.

content.subject: Fix withTimeout not observing caller's own cancellation
content.description: TODOS.md line 608. Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. Wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancelling the caller settles TimeoutGate early (same shape as JJSnapshotGate.run). Broad blast radius (WorkroomStatusResolver, BranchResolver, JJSnapshotGate's own use) - needs task #7's test harness in place first to verify the fix observably.

let app = launchedApp()
    XCTAssertTrue(app.wait(for: .runningForeground, timeout: 10))

    let bell = app.buttons["activityBar.notifications"]
    XCTAssertTrue(bell.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
    assertLabel(bell, equals: "Notifications, 7 unread")

    let chip = workroomChips(app).firstMatch
    XCTAssertTrue(chip.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
    chip.rightClick()
    app.menuItems["Delete Workroom…"].click()
    let confirm = app.sheets.buttons["Delete"]
    XCTAssertTrue(confirm.waitForExistence(timeout: 4), "the delete confirmation should appear")
    // The sheet's own presentation animation can leave its button existing-but-not-yet-hittable for
    // a beat; clicking during that window has landed as a no-op click-through in practice.
    let hittable = XCTNSPredicateExpectation(
      predicate: NSPredicate(format: "isHittable == true"), object: confirm)
    XCTAssertEqual(XCTWaiter().wait(for: [hittable], timeout: 4), .completed)
    confirm.click()

content.description: TODOS.md line 608. Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. Wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancelling the caller settles TimeoutGate early (same shape as JJSnapshotGate.run). Broad blast radius (WorkroomStatusResolver, BranchResolver, JJSnapshotGate's own use) - needs task #7's test harness in place first to verify the fix observably.

let chip = workroomChips(app).firstMatch
    XCTAssertTrue(chip.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
    chip.rightClick()
    app.menuItems["Delete Workroom…"].click()
    let confirm = app.sheets.buttons["Delete"]
    XCTAssertTrue(confirm.waitForExistence(timeout: 4), "the delete confirmation should appear")
    // The sheet's own presentation animation can leave its button existing-but-not-yet-hittable for
    // a beat; clicking during that window has landed as a no-op click-through in practice.
    let hittable = XCTNSPredicateExpectation(
      predicate: NSPredicate(format: "isHittable == true"), object: confirm)
    XCTAssertEqual(XCTWaiter().wait(for: [hittable], timeout: 4), .completed)
    confirm.click()

    assertLabel(bell, equals: "Notifications", timeout: 8)

72	  /// Poll a condition on the main actor, letting queued teardown/reload work run. Bounded so a broken
73	  /// condition fails the assertion instead of hanging.
74	  private func waitUntil(
75	    _ condition: () -> Bool, _ message: String, file: StaticString = #filePath, line: UInt = #line
76	  ) async {
77	    for _ in 0..<200 {
78	      if condition() { return }
79	      try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 2_000_000)  // 2ms; up to ~400ms total
80	    }
81	    XCTFail(message, file: file, line: line)
82	  }
83	
84	  // MARK: - The reload race (the reported bug)
85	
86	  /// The core bug: after a workroom is optimistically deleted, a concurrent reload whose `list`
87	  /// snapshot was taken BEFORE the teardown persisted must NOT resurrect it (issue #116).
88	  func testStaleReloadDoesNotResurrectDeletedWorkroom() async {
89	    let a = workroom("a")
90	    let b = workroom("b")
91	    let fake = DeleteRaceFakeCLI()
92	    fake.listResult = [project([a, b])]
93	    let store = makeStore(fake)
94	    await store.reload()
95	    XCTAssertEqual(workroomNames(store), ["a", "b"])
96	
97	    // Delete `a`. Its teardown is gated (never released here), so `a` stays tombstoned throughout.
98	    store.deleteWorkroom(a, in: project([a, b]))
99	    XCTAssertEqual(workroomNames(store), ["b"], "optimistic removal drops it immediately")
100	    XCTAssertTrue(store.deletingWorkrooms.contains(targetID("a")))
101	
102	    // A concurrent flow (another create/delete/refresh) reloads while `a`'s teardown is still in
103	    // flight — and its `list` snapshot is STALE, still listing `a` (config not yet updated).
104	    fake.listResult = [project([a, b])]
105	    await store.reload()
106	    XCTAssertEqual(
107	      workroomNames(store), ["b"],
108	      "a stale reload must NOT bring the deleted workroom back")
109	
110	    // Let the teardown finish; the tombstone lifts and a now-fresh list stays clean.
111	    fake.allowDelete = true
112	    await waitUntil({ store.deletingWorkrooms.isEmpty }, "tombstone should clear after teardown")
113	    fake.listResult = [project([b])]
114	    await store.reload()
115	    XCTAssertEqual(workroomNames(store), ["b"])
116	  }
117	
118	  /// A FAILED teardown must restore the workroom: the tombstone is cleared and the reload brings it
119	  /// back (it still exists on disk / in config).
120	  func testFailedTeardownRestoresWorkroom() async {
121	    let a = workroom("a")
122	    let b = workroom("b")
123	    let fake = DeleteRaceFakeCLI()
124	    fake.listResult = [project([a, b])]
125	    fake.deleteFails = true
126	    let store = makeStore(fake)
127	    await store.reload()
128	
129	    store.deleteWorkroom(a, in: project([a, b]))
130	    XCTAssertEqual(workroomNames(store), ["b"], "optimistic removal")
131	    await waitUntil({ fake.deleteStarted }, "teardown should start")
132	
133	    // The teardown fails; config still has `a`, so it must reappear once the tombstone clears.
134	    fake.allowDelete = true
135	    await waitUntil(
136	      { self.workroomNames(store) == ["a", "b"] }, "failed teardown restores the workroom")
137	    XCTAssertFalse(store.deletingWorkrooms.contains(targetID("a")), "tombstone cleared on failure")
138	  }

content.subject: Fix withTimeout not observing caller's own cancellation
content.description: TODOS.md line 608. Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. Wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancelling the caller settles TimeoutGate early (same shape as JJSnapshotGate.run). Broad blast radius (WorkroomStatusResolver, BranchResolver, JJSnapshotGate's own use) - needs task #7's test harness in place first to verify the fix observably.

// Opening it dismisses it (`AppStore.openTerminal`'s `notifications.dismiss(notifID:)`) — it must
    // not still be in the backlog. Re-open the popover (clicking a row closes it) to check.
    bell.click()
    popover = app.popovers.firstMatch
    XCTAssertTrue(popover.waitForExistence(timeout: 4))
    XCTAssertFalse(
      popover.buttons.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label CONTAINS 'Live OSC Ping'")).firstMatch
        .exists,
      "opening the notification should have dismissed it")
  }

  /// Deleting a workroom must withdraw its pending notifications (`AppStore.reapTargetLocally` calls
  /// `notifications.removeForTarget`) — the fixture's whole 5-entry seeded backlog belongs to the
  /// single auto-selected workroom (see `UITestFixture.notifications`), so deleting the only workroom
  /// must drop the bell to its empty, disabled state, not merely decrement it.
  func testDeletingAWorkroomWithdrawsItsNotifications() throws {
    let app = launchedApp()
    XCTAssertTrue(app.wait(for: .runningForeground, timeout: 10))

    let bell = app.buttons["activityBar.notifications"]
    XCTAssertTrue(bell.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
    assertLabel(bell, equals: "Notifications, 7 unread")

    let chip = workroomChips(app).firstMatch
    XCTAssertTrue(chip.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
    chip.rightClick()
    app.menuItems["Delete Workroom…"].click()
    let confirm = app.sheets.buttons["Delete"]
    XCTAssertTrue(confirm.waitForExistence(timeout: 4), "the delete confirmation should appear")
    // The sheet's own presentation animation can leave its button existing-but-not-yet-hittable for
    // a beat; clicking during that window has landed as a no-op click-through in practice.
    let hittable = XCTNSPredicateExpectation(
      predicate: NSPredicate(format: "isHittable == true"), object: confirm)
    XCTAssertEqual(XCTWaiter().wait(for: [hittable], timeout: 4), .completed)
    confirm.click()
    print(
      "DEBUG t=0.3 bell.label=\(bell.label) alerts=\(app.alerts.count) sheets=\(app.sheets.count)")
    Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.7)
    print(
      "DEBUG t=1.0 bell.label=\(bell.label) alerts=\(app.alerts.count) sheets=\(app.sheets.count)")
    Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 1)

2171	**What:** Replace `AsyncImage` in `AvatarView` (`Views/Avatar.swift`) with a small loader that reads the
2172	HTTP status, caches decoded images in memory, caches genuine 404s, and retries transient failures.
2173	
2174	**Why:** the shipped mitigation (`AvatarImageFailures`) is a session set of URLs whose load *failed* —
2175	and `AsyncImage`'s `.failure` phase carries an error, not a status, so "this author has no Gravatar"
2176	and "the network dropped" are indistinguishable. The set is therefore cleared on app activation, which
2177	bounds the damage but means an offline scroll shows initials until the user comes back to the app. A
2178	status-aware loader removes the ambiguity, and gets image caching (no flicker on re-realization) for
2179	free. Gravatar is requested with `d=404` on purpose, so a miss really is a 404 — the information is
2180	there, `AsyncImage` just doesn't expose it.
2181	
2182	**Current state:** `AvatarImageFailures.shared` + the `.failure` branch in `AvatarView.body`. Covered
2183	by no test: `AsyncImage` offers no injection seam, which is itself part of the argument for replacing it
2184	(a hand-rolled loader is testable behind a `URLProtocol` stub).

2187	`.loadRemoteAvatars` privacy gate exactly as it is — no request may be issued when it's off. Bound the

HTTP status, caches decoded images in memory, caches genuine 404s, and retries transient failures.

**Why:** the shipped mitigation (`AvatarImageFailures`) is a session set of URLs whose load *failed* —
and `AsyncImage`'s `.failure` phase carries an error, not a status, so "this author has no Gravatar"
and "the network dropped" are indistinguishable. The set is therefore cleared on app activation, which
bounds the damage but means an offline scroll shows initials until the user comes back to the app. A
status-aware loader removes the ambiguity, and gets image caching (no flicker on re-realization) for
free. Gravatar is requested with `d=404` on purpose, so a miss really is a 404 — the information is
there, `AsyncImage` just doesn't expose it.

**Current state:** `AvatarImageFailures.shared` + the `.failure` branch in `AvatarView.body`. Covered
by no test: `AsyncImage` offers no injection seam, which is itself part of the argument for replacing it
(a hand-rolled loader is testable behind a `URLProtocol` stub).

**How to start:** `AvatarView.body`'s image branch and the `AvatarSubject.imageURL` contract. Keep the
`.loadRemoteAvatars` privacy gate exactly as it is — no request may be issued when it's off. Bound the
image cache (count or bytes); Gravatar/GitHub avatars are 16–54 px, so it stays small.

**Depends on:** nothing (the lazy History list that made repeated loads visible has landed).

**Priority:** P3 — the current mitigation covers the common case; this is the correct version.

### `FilesPanel` renders up to 4000 rows eagerly (macapp) — WORKROOM-2B follow-up

**What:** `Views/FilesPanel.swift:58-60` builds every visible tree row in an eager `VStack`, capped at
`FileTreeModel.renderCap = 4000`, and each row holds `@EnvironmentObject store` + `@ObservedObject
model`.

**Why:** this is the third instance of the pattern that produced the WORKROOM-2B App Hang — eager stack
plus per-row observation of a publishing object — and its cap is 20× the Changes panel's 200. The
History pane took >2 seconds of main thread at ~1000 rows of comparable per-row work.

**Why it is NOT P1:** unmeasured. No hang report names Files, and `FileTreeModel` publishes far less
often than `TerminalSessions` did (tree loads and expand/collapse, not terminal output), so the
high-frequency trigger that made History fatal may simply not exist here. Tree rows also carry
expand/collapse state, which lazy stacks handle less predictably than fixed-height list rows.

**How to start:** measure before changing anything — add a `#if DEBUG bodyPasses` counter to the row
(same shape as `HistoryRow`/`ChangedFileRow`) and count passes per `FileTreeModel` publish with a large
expanded tree. If the number is large, the fix is the one this branch established: hoist the selection

**Priority:** P3 — structural risk, no measured symptom.

12	/// "is my commit the focused changeset?", and `TerminalSessions` republishes on every terminal
13	/// title update and activity pulse — so while an agent streamed, EVERY row body re-ran, over an
14	/// eager `VStack` holding the whole loaded window.
15	///

17	/// model test cannot see them:
18	///
19	/// 1. **A terminal pulse rebuilds nothing.** `testTerminalPulseBurstRebuildsNoRows` fails on the
20	///    pre-fix code (one rebuild per row per pulse) and is the test that would have caught the hang.
21	/// 2. **Selection and content changes still DO rebuild.** The equality gate that gives us (1) can
22	///    just as easily freeze a row's contents; `testSelectionChangeRebuildsRows` and

4	/// The live data source behind the inspector's **Files** section: lists the selected target's
5	/// working tree (via git, falling back to jj), builds the tree, tracks which directories are
6	/// expanded, and reloads when the filesystem changes. All the data-shaping is delegated to the pure
7	/// helpers in `FileTree.swift`; this owns the I/O + observable state.
8	///
9	/// `@MainActor` so SwiftUI reads it directly; the listing itself runs off-main inside
10	/// `StatusCommandRunner` (it drains the child's pipes on background queues), so the main actor only
11	/// touches the small parsed result.
12	@MainActor
13	final class FileTreeModel: ObservableObject {
14	  enum State: Equatable {
15	    /// No target selected.
16	    case idle
17	    /// Listing for the first time (no tree yet to show).
18	    case loading
19	    /// `roots` is current (may be empty — an empty repo).
20	    case loaded
21	    /// Not a git/jj repo, or the tool is missing — nothing to list.
22	    case unavailable
23	  }
24	
25	  /// The sorted root nodes of the current target's tree.
26	  @Published private(set) var roots: [FileNode] = []
27	  @Published private(set) var state: State = .idle
28	  /// Expanded directory paths. Reset on target switch; the panel toggles entries.
29	  @Published var expanded: Set<String> = []
30	
31	  /// Max rows the panel renders at once (a guard for pathologically large trees); the panel notes
32	  /// any overflow rather than silently truncating.
33	  static let renderCap = 4000
34	
35	  /// The visible rows for the current tree + expansion — what the panel iterates.
36	  var rows: [FileTreeRow] { FileTreeBuilder.flatten(roots, expanded: expanded) }
37	
38	  private var currentPath: String?
39	  /// The owning project's root for `currentPath` (nil for a root target, where it equals
40	  /// `currentPath` itself) — threaded into `list` to key `JJSnapshotGate` for the jj branch, the
41	  /// same way `AppStore.projectRoot(forTarget:)` feeds `DiffResolver`.
42	  private var currentProjectRoot: String?
43	  private let runner: StatusCommandRunning
44	  private let gate: JJSnapshotGate
45	  private var watcher: WorkroomFileWatcher?
46	  private var loadTask: Task<Void, Never>?
47	
48	  init(runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(), gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared) {
49	    self.runner = runner
50	    self.gate = gate
51	  }
52	
53	  deinit {
54	    loadTask?.cancel()
55	    watcher?.stop()
56	  }
57	
58	  /// Point the model at a target directory (a workroom/project root), or `nil` to clear. Starts
59	  /// watching it and lists it. No-op if already on this path (so re-renders don't re-list).
60	  /// `projectRoot` is the owning project's root (nil ⇒ falls back to `path` itself, e.g. for a root
61	  /// target where they're the same) — see `currentProjectRoot`.
62	  func activate(path: String?, projectRoot: String? = nil) {
63	    guard path != currentPath else { return }
64	    loadTask?.cancel()
65	    currentPath = path
66	    currentProjectRoot = projectRoot
67	    expanded = []
68	    // A nil path (nothing selected / Files section hidden) or a missing directory (a vanished
69	    // workroom) clears the tree without spawning git/jj or a watcher.
70	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
71	    let exists =
72	      path.map { FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: $0, isDirectory: &isDir) } ?? false
73	    guard let path, exists, isDir.boolValue else {
74	      watcher?.stop()
75	      watcher = nil
76	      roots = []
77	      state = path == nil ? .idle : .unavailable
78	      return
79	    }
80	    startWatching(path)
81	    state = .loading
82	    roots = []
83	    reload()
84	  }
85	
86	  /// Re-list the current target (a manual refresh, or after a watched filesystem change). Keeps the
87	  /// existing tree visible while the new listing runs.
88	  func reload() {
89	    guard let path = currentPath else { return }
90	    let projectRoot = currentProjectRoot
91	    loadTask?.cancel()
92	    loadTask = Task { [weak self] in
93	      guard let self else { return }
94	      let result = await FileTreeModel.list(
95	        path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot, runner: self.runner, gate: self.gate)
96	      guard !Task.isCancelled, self.currentPath == path else { return }
97	      switch result {
98	      case .listing(let paths):
99	        self.roots = FileTreeBuilder.build(from: paths)
100	        self.state = .loaded
101	      case .unavailable:
102	        self.roots = []
103	        self.state = .unavailable
104	      case .interrupted:
105	        // An external kill, not evidence `path` stopped being a repo — leave whatever tree/state
106	        // is already showing alone (the same "keep the existing tree visible" contract this
107	        // function already promises while a listing is in flight) rather than blanking it.
108	        break
109	      }
110	    }
111	  }

1	import AppKit
2	import XCTest
3	
4	/// Shared "let the SwiftUI/AppKit run loop catch up" waiter for the WORKROOM-2B/2T/2S app-hang
5	/// regression suites (`ChangedFileRowInvalidationTests`, `HistoryRowInvalidationTests`,
6	/// `DiffViewerLazyRenderingTests`, `AgentResumeCoordinatorTests`).
7	///
8	/// Pumps the run loop in short slices, forcing layout each time, until either `condition` returns
9	/// true or `seconds` elapses — whichever comes first. `condition` defaults to `{ false }`, which
10	/// makes this behave exactly like the old per-file busy-wait (always burns the full `seconds`):
11	/// some call sites are waiting out an unrelated async race (e.g. a status probe) rather than a
12	/// render they can observe, and forcing a fabricated condition onto those would be worse than no
13	/// condition at all. Pass a real condition wherever one exists (e.g. a `bodyPasses` counter tied
14	/// to the assertion that follows) to return as soon as the work is actually done instead of always
15	/// paying the ceiling.
16	extension XCTestCase {
17	  @MainActor
18	  func settle(_ view: NSView, seconds: TimeInterval = 0.6, until condition: () -> Bool = { false })
19	  {
20	    let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(seconds)
21	    while Date() < deadline {
22	      view.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
23	      RunLoop.current.run(until: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.02))
24	      if condition() { break }
25	    }
26	    view.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
27	  }
28	
29	  /// View-less overload for model/coordinator-layer tests with nothing to lay out (e.g.
30	  /// `AgentResumeCoordinatorTests`) — same poll-until-condition-or-ceiling mechanism, without the
31	  /// `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()` half.
32	  @MainActor
33	  func settle(_ seconds: TimeInterval = 0.5, until condition: () -> Bool = { false }) {
34	    let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(seconds)
35	    while Date() < deadline {
36	      RunLoop.current.run(mode: .default, before: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.01))
37	      if condition() { break }
38	    }
39	  }
40	}

Detection of staleness already happens for free via the existing per-workroom status sweep (confirmed in code: WorkroomStatusResolver/.staleWorkingCopy already surfaces for any workroom, focused or not). The remaining gap - attributing WHICH sibling workroom caused it - needs op-log correlation across workspaces, a real design task, not a quick fix. Building a rushed repair button here would contradict the project's own explicit deferral and ship an unreviewed write action pre-release. Flagging to Joel rather than proceeding.

content.subject: Add injection seam to resolveGit/resolveJJ + N-in-flight concurrency-cap test
content.description: TODOS.md line 1024. WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit/resolveJJ currently call GitProvider().workingStatus(root:)/native jj core directly, bypassing the existing StatusCommandRunning injection point. Add a seam, then write an actor-gate test on runLocalSweep/runCISweep's cap-bounded withTaskGroup fan-out (AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:457-529) asserting concurrent local-status probes never exceed cap. Must land before task #8 (withTimeout fix) so that fix has a real test harness underneath it.
content.activeForm: Adding status-resolver injection seam and concurrency test

content.subject: Fix withTimeout not observing caller's own cancellation
content.description: TODOS.md line 608. Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. Wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancelling the caller settles TimeoutGate early (same shape as JJSnapshotGate.run). Broad blast radius (WorkroomStatusResolver, BranchResolver, JJSnapshotGate's own use) - needs task #7's test harness in place first to verify the fix observably.

1	import AppKit

3	import XCTest

5	@testable import Workroom
6	
7	/// Measures the WORKROOM-2B candidate flagged in TODOS.md for `Views/FilesPanel.swift`:
8	/// `FileTreeRowView` holds BOTH `@EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore` (used only inside tap/menu
9	/// closures, never read in the rendered body) and `@ObservedObject var model: FileTreeModel`, over
10	/// an eager `VStack` capped at 4000 rows — the same shape that turned per-row avatar work into a
11	/// 2-second History-pane stall. The TODO's own instruction: measure before changing anything.
12	///
13	/// Harness mirrors `HistoryRowInvalidationTests` (offscreen `NSHostingView`, the shared `settle`
14	/// waiter) — `FileTreeModel` is hosted standalone (not `store.fileTree`), fed by a fake
15	/// `StatusCommandRunning` so no real `git`/`jj` process is ever spawned.
16	@MainActor
17	final class FilesPanelInvalidationTests: XCTestCase {
18	
19	  // MARK: harness
20	
21	  /// Returns a fixed `git ls-files -z` result for however many paths were configured; the `jj`
22	  /// branch is never reached because git always succeeds first.
23	  private final class FixedGitListRunner: StatusCommandRunning, @unchecked Sendable {
24	    var paths: [String] = []
25	    func run(_ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String, timeout: TimeInterval)
26	      async -> CommandResult
27	    {
28	      CommandResult(
29	        stdout: paths.joined(separator: "\0") + "\0", stderr: "", exitCode: 0, timedOut: false)
30	    }
31	  }
32	
33	  private var tempDirs: [String] = []
34	
35	  override func tearDown() {
36	    for d in tempDirs { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(atPath: d) }
37	    tempDirs = []
38	    super.tearDown()
39	  }
40	
41	  /// A real, empty throwaway directory — `FileTreeModel.activate` requires the path to exist on
42	  /// disk, but the listing itself is entirely faked, so nothing inside it is ever read.
43	  private func throwawayDir() -> String {
44	    let path = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "wr-filespanel-\(UUID().uuidString)"
45	    try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: path, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
46	    tempDirs.append(path)
47	    return path
48	  }
49	
50	  /// A `FileTreeModel` activated against `count` FLAT (no subdirectories) synthetic files, so every
51	  /// one is a visible row with no expansion needed — directly exercising "renders up to 4000 rows
52	  /// eagerly", not the (also-eager, but separately gated) directory-expansion path.
53	  private func activatedModel(fileCount count: Int) async -> FileTreeModel {
54	    let runner = FixedGitListRunner()
55	    runner.paths = (0..<count).map { "file-\($0).txt" }
56	    let model = FileTreeModel(runner: runner)
57	    let path = throwawayDir()
58	    model.activate(path: path)
59	    await settle(until: { model.state == .loaded })
60	    return model
61	  }
62	
63	  /// A store with an active selection (so `FilesPanel` clears its "No open terminal" placeholder)
64	  /// but otherwise uninvolved with the file tree — the model under test is hosted standalone.
65	  private func makeStore() -> AppStore {
66	    let store = AppStore()
67	    store.terminals.makeView = { _, cwd, _ in GhosttySurfaceView(workingDirectory: cwd) }
68	    let projectPath = "/files-invalidation"
69	    store.projects = [
70	      Project(
71	        path: projectPath, vcs: "git",
72	        workrooms: [
73	          Workroom(
74	            name: "solo", path: "\(projectPath)/solo", vcsName: "workroom/solo", warnings: [])
75	        ])
76	    ]
77	    let target = store.target(for: .workroom(project: projectPath, name: "solo"))!
78	    _ = store.terminals.addTab(for: target)
79	    store.selectedTargetID = .workroom(project: projectPath, name: "solo")
80	    return store
81	  }
82	
83	  /// Host the real `FilesPanel` offscreen, directly over the given model (not `store.fileTree`).
84	  private func host(_ store: AppStore, _ model: FileTreeModel) -> (NSWindow, NSView) {
85	    let root = FilesPanel(model: model)
86	      .environmentObject(store)
87	      .environmentObject(store.notifications)
88	      .frame(width: 280, height: 400)
89	    let hosting = NSHostingView(rootView: root)
90	    hosting.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 280, height: 400)
91	    let window = NSWindow(
92	      contentRect: hosting.frame, styleMask: [.titled], backing: .buffered, defer: false)
93	    window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false
94	    window.contentView = hosting
95	    window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
96	    return (window, hosting)
97	  }
98	
99	  // MARK: measurements
100	
101	  /// The scale question the TODO poses literally: does the eager `VStack` build every row of a
102	  /// large tree (unlike a lazy list, which would build only the viewport)?
103	  func testLargeTreeBuildsEveryVisibleRow() async throws {
104	    let model = await activatedModel(fileCount: 1000)
105	    let store = makeStore()
106	    FileTreeRowView.bodyPasses = 0
107	    let (window, view) = host(store, model)
108	    defer { window.close() }
109	    settle(view)
110	
111	    XCTAssertEqual(
112	      FileTreeRowView.bodyPasses, 1000,
113	      "a 280×400 panel shows ~15 rows, so building all 1000 confirms the VStack is eager — matching "
114	        + "the Changes/History/Diff pattern, not yet fixed here")
115	  }
116	
117	  /// The actual WORKROOM-2B mechanism: does a publish of `AppStore` that says NOTHING about the file
118	  /// tree still rebuild every row? `store` is read only inside `FileTreeRowView`'s tap/menu closures
119	  /// today, never in its rendered body — if that's still true, this MUST be zero.
120	  func testUnrelatedAppStorePublishRebuildsRows() async throws {
121	    let model = await activatedModel(fileCount: 200)
122	    let store = makeStore()
123	    let (window, view) = host(store, model)
124	    defer { window.close() }
125	    settle(view)
126	    XCTAssertGreaterThan(
127	      FileTreeRowView.bodyPasses, 0, "the fixture must actually render file rows")
128	
129	    FileTreeRowView.bodyPasses = 0
130	    // Reassigning a `@Published` property fires `objectWillChange` regardless of value equality —
131	    // this says nothing whatsoever about the file tree.
132	    for _ in 0..<10 { store.isLoading.toggle() }
133	    settle(view)
134	
135	    XCTAssertEqual(
136	      FileTreeRowView.bodyPasses, 0,
137	      "an AppStore publish unrelated to the file tree rebuilt \(FileTreeRowView.bodyPasses) row "
138	        + "passes — this is the WORKROOM-2B mechanism: `store` is read only inside this row's "
139	        + "closures, never its body, so ANY AppStore publish (title/activity/notifications/status, "
140	        + "all far higher-frequency than a file-tree reload) shouldn't touch it at all")
141	  }
142	
143	  /// The model's OWN publish, unrelated to any row's own content: does toggling ONE directory's
144	  /// expansion (which flips `FileTreeModel.expanded`, a single `@Published` `Set` shared by every
145	  /// row) rebuild siblings that didn't change? No equality gate exists today, so this is expected to
146	  /// be nonzero — the question this test exists to pin is HOW MANY, as the baseline a future fix's
147	  /// regression test would tighten.
148	  func testTogglingOneDirectoryRebuildsSiblingRows() async throws {
149	    let runner = FixedGitListRunner()
150	    runner.paths = ["dir/a.txt"] + (0..<200).map { "file-\($0).txt" }
151	    let model = FileTreeModel(runner: runner)
152	    let path = throwawayDir()
153	    model.activate(path: path)
154	    await settle(until: { model.state == .loaded })
155	    let store = makeStore()
156	    let (window, view) = host(store, model)
157	    defer { window.close() }
158	    settle(view)
159	    guard let dir = model.roots.first(where: { $0.isDirectory }) else {
160	      return XCTFail("fixture must include a directory row to toggle")
161	    }
162	
163	    FileTreeRowView.bodyPasses = 0
164	    model.toggle(dir)
165	    settle(view)
166	
167	    // Not a regression assertion (no fix has landed) — just proving the measurement mechanism sees
168	    // a real, nonzero effect, so the two tests above aren't passing by accident (nothing rendering).

content.subject: Add Makefile/CI test-invariant meta-check (script tier)
content.description: TODOS.md line 1051: pin APP_UITEST_FLAGS skip list (post-flake-fix contents) and confirm release/nightly CI workflows actually invoke app-test, as a dependency-free script alongside Scripts/build-helper_test.sh / channel-helper_test.sh (run via make app-test-scripts) — NOT a new XCTest class (that framing was corrected away in the TODO). Must run after task #3 lands so the skip list it pins is current.

content.subject: Fix git diff showing only one side when file is both staged and re-modified
content.description: TODOS.md line 1272, VCS-foundation eng-review finding. Self-contained real bug, no dependencies on other items in this batch.

content.subject: Fix jj sibling-workspace staleness after a rebase
content.description: TODOS.md line 782, VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up. jj projects only; wrong-workroom errors are rare but confusing. Self-contained.

metadata.blocked_reason: This TODO's real deliverable is a repair action (jj workspace update-stale / Workspace::recover), and the project's OWN TODOS.md (line 1352, 'Offer to repair a stale jj working copy') explicitly defers that: 'every VCS write belongs to the Phase-2 write-actions chunk (its own confirmation + undo story), not to a status probe.' Detection of staleness already happens for free via the existing per-workroom status sweep (confirmed in code: WorkroomStatusResolver/.staleWorkingCopy already surfaces for any workroom, focused or not). The remaining gap - attributing WHICH sibling workroom caused it - needs op-log correlation across workspaces, a real design task, not a quick fix. Building a rushed repair button here would contradict the project's own explicit deferral and ship an unreviewed write action pre-release. Flagging to Joel rather than proceeding.

content.subject: Add injection seam to resolveGit/resolveJJ + N-in-flight concurrency-cap test
content.description: TODOS.md line 1024. WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit/resolveJJ currently call GitProvider().workingStatus(root:)/native jj core directly, bypassing the existing StatusCommandRunning injection point. Add a seam, then write an actor-gate test on runLocalSweep/runCISweep's cap-bounded withTaskGroup fan-out (AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:457-529) asserting concurrent local-status probes never exceed cap. Must land before task #8 (withTimeout fix) so that fix has a real test harness underneath it.
content.activeForm: Adding status-resolver injection seam and concurrency test

content.subject: Fix withTimeout not observing caller's own cancellation
content.description: TODOS.md line 608. Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. Wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancelling the caller settles TimeoutGate early (same shape as JJSnapshotGate.run). Broad blast radius (WorkroomStatusResolver, BranchResolver, JJSnapshotGate's own use) - needs task #7's test harness in place first to verify the fix observably.

content.subject: Add deferred UI workflow tests (notification-path coverage)
content.description: TODOS.md line 2106: smoke + opportunistic suites cover the basics but some notification-path UI workflows lack dedicated tests. Needs machine-driving permission (UI test run) - batch with task #3.

content.subject: Measure then fix FilesPanel eager 4000-row render + status-aware avatar loader
content.description: TODOS.md lines 2187 and 2162, both P3 "no measured symptom yet." Measure first (Instruments/timing) before changing - otherwise the perf commit is unfalsifiable. Two related WORKROOM-2B follow-ups, likely one commit or two small sequential ones.

1	import AppKit
2	import SwiftUI
3	import XCTest
4	
5	@testable import Workroom
6	
7	/// Measures the WORKROOM-2B candidate flagged in TODOS.md for `Views/FilesPanel.swift`:
8	/// `FileTreeRowView` holds BOTH `@EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore` (used only inside tap/menu
9	/// closures, never read in the rendered body) and `@ObservedObject var model: FileTreeModel`, over
10	/// an eager `VStack` capped at 4000 rows — the same shape that turned per-row avatar work into a
11	/// 2-second History-pane stall. The TODO's own instruction: measure before changing anything.
12	///
13	/// Harness mirrors `HistoryRowInvalidationTests` (offscreen `NSHostingView`, the shared `settle`
14	/// waiter) — `FileTreeModel` is hosted standalone (not `store.fileTree`), fed by a fake
15	/// `StatusCommandRunning` so no real `git`/`jj` process is ever spawned.
16	@MainActor
17	final class FilesPanelInvalidationTests: XCTestCase {
18	
19	  // MARK: harness
20	
21	  /// Returns a fixed `git ls-files -z` result for however many paths were configured; the `jj`
22	  /// branch is never reached because git always succeeds first.
23	  private final class FixedGitListRunner: StatusCommandRunning, @unchecked Sendable {
24	    var paths: [String] = []
25	    func run(_ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String, timeout: TimeInterval)
26	      async -> CommandResult
27	    {
28	      CommandResult(
29	        stdout: paths.joined(separator: "\0") + "\0", stderr: "", exitCode: 0, timedOut: false)
30	    }
31	  }
32	
33	  private var tempDirs: [String] = []
34	
35	  override func tearDown() {
36	    for d in tempDirs { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(atPath: d) }
37	    tempDirs = []
38	    super.tearDown()
39	  }
40	
41	  /// A real, empty throwaway directory — `FileTreeModel.activate` requires the path to exist on
42	  /// disk, but the listing itself is entirely faked, so nothing inside it is ever read.
43	  private func throwawayDir() -> String {
44	    let path = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "wr-filespanel-\(UUID().uuidString)"
45	    try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: path, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
46	    tempDirs.append(path)
47	    return path
48	  }
49	
50	  /// `settle`'s `RunLoop.current` pump (built for letting AppKit/SwiftUI layout catch up) never gives
51	  /// `FileTreeModel.reload`'s unstructured `Task` a turn in this plain-XCTest hosting context — a
52	  /// real `Task.sleep` poll does, mirroring `AppStoreDeleteRaceTests.waitUntil`.
53	  private func awaitLoaded(_ model: FileTreeModel) async {
54	    for _ in 0..<200 {
55	      if model.state == .loaded { return }
56	      try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 2_000_000)
57	    }
58	  }
59	
60	  /// A `FileTreeModel` activated against `count` FLAT (no subdirectories) synthetic files, so every
61	  /// one is a visible row with no expansion needed — directly exercising "renders up to 4000 rows
62	  /// eagerly", not the (also-eager, but separately gated) directory-expansion path.
63	  private func activatedModel(fileCount count: Int) async -> FileTreeModel {
64	    let runner = FixedGitListRunner()
65	    runner.paths = (0..<count).map { "file-\($0).txt" }
66	    let model = FileTreeModel(runner: runner)
67	    model.activate(path: throwawayDir())
68	    await awaitLoaded(model)
69	    return model
70	  }
71	
72	  /// A store with an active selection (so `FilesPanel` clears its "No open terminal" placeholder)
73	  /// but otherwise uninvolved with the file tree — the model under test is hosted standalone.
74	  private func makeStore() -> AppStore {
75	    let store = AppStore()
76	    store.terminals.makeView = { _, cwd, _ in GhosttySurfaceView(workingDirectory: cwd) }
77	    let projectPath = "/files-invalidation"
78	    store.projects = [
79	      Project(
80	        path: projectPath, vcs: "git",
81	        workrooms: [
82	          Workroom(
83	            name: "solo", path: "\(projectPath)/solo", vcsName: "workroom/solo", warnings: [])
84	        ])
85	    ]
86	    let target = store.target(for: .workroom(project: projectPath, name: "solo"))!
87	    _ = store.terminals.addTab(for: target)
88	    store.selectedTargetID = .workroom(project: projectPath, name: "solo")
89	    // Not fired automatically by the above in this bare harness (no real window/focus event drives
90	    // it) — `FilesPanel`'s placeholder gate (`store.inspectorTargetID`) depends on it directly.
91	    store.refreshSelectionHasTabs()
92	    return store
93	  }
94	
95	  /// Host the real `FilesPanel` offscreen, directly over the given model (not `store.fileTree`).
96	  private func host(_ store: AppStore, _ model: FileTreeModel) -> (NSWindow, NSView) {
97	    let root = FilesPanel(model: model)
98	      .environmentObject(store)
99	      .environmentObject(store.notifications)

### Status-aware avatar image loader (macapp) — WORKROOM-2B follow-up

**What:** Replace `AsyncImage` in `AvatarView` (`Views/Avatar.swift`) with a small loader that reads the
HTTP status, caches decoded images in memory, caches genuine 404s, and retries transient failures.

**Why:** the shipped mitigation (`AvatarImageFailures`) is a session set of URLs whose load *failed* —
and `AsyncImage`'s `.failure` phase carries an error, not a status, so "this author has no Gravatar"
and "the network dropped" are indistinguishable. The set is therefore cleared on app activation, which
bounds the damage but means an offline scroll shows initials until the user comes back to the app. A
status-aware loader removes the ambiguity, and gets image caching (no flicker on re-realization) for
free. Gravatar is requested with `d=404` on purpose, so a miss really is a 404 — the information is
there, `AsyncImage` just doesn't expose it.

**Current state:** `AvatarImageFailures.shared` + the `.failure` branch in `AvatarView.body`. Covered
by no test: `AsyncImage` offers no injection seam, which is itself part of the argument for replacing it
(a hand-rolled loader is testable behind a `URLProtocol` stub).

**How to start:** `AvatarView.body`'s image branch and the `AvatarSubject.imageURL` contract. Keep the
`.loadRemoteAvatars` privacy gate exactly as it is — no request may be issued when it's off. Bound the
image cache (count or bytes); Gravatar/GitHub avatars are 16–54 px, so it stays small.

**Depends on:** nothing (the lazy History list that made repeated loads visible has landed).

**Priority:** P3 — the current mitigation covers the common case; this is the correct version.

### `FilesPanel` renders up to 4000 rows eagerly (macapp) — WORKROOM-2B follow-up

**What:** `Views/FilesPanel.swift:58-60` builds every visible tree row in an eager `VStack`, capped at
`FileTreeModel.renderCap = 4000`, and each row holds `@EnvironmentObject store` + `@ObservedObject
model`.

**Why:** this is the third instance of the pattern that produced the WORKROOM-2B App Hang — eager stack
plus per-row observation of a publishing object — and its cap is 20× the Changes panel's 200. The
History pane took >2 seconds of main thread at ~1000 rows of comparable per-row work.

**Why it is NOT P1:** unmeasured. No hang report names Files, and `FileTreeModel` publishes far less
often than `TerminalSessions` did (tree loads and expand/collapse, not terminal output), so the
high-frequency trigger that made History fatal may simply not exist here. Tree rows also carry
expand/collapse state, which lazy stacks handle less predictably than fixed-height list rows.

**How to start:** measure before changing anything — add a `#if DEBUG bodyPasses` counter to the row
(same shape as `HistoryRow`/`ChangedFileRow`) and count passes per `FileTreeModel` publish with a large
expanded tree. If the number is large, the fix is the one this branch established: hoist the selection
lookup into the panel, give the row an `Equatable` gate, and switch the stack to `LazyVStack` (only if
the rows are fixed-height — see the comment at `Views/DiffViewer.swift`'s `unifiedBody` for when lazy
is wrong).

**Depends on:** nothing; the counter harness and the pattern both exist now.

**Priority:** P3 — structural risk, no measured symptom.

### Status-aware avatar image loader (macapp) — FIXED

**What:** Replace `AsyncImage` in `AvatarView` (`Views/Avatar.swift`) with a small loader that reads the
HTTP status, caches decoded images in memory, caches genuine 404s, and retries transient failures.

**Fixed:** `AvatarImageLoader` — an actor-free `@MainActor` class with an injectable `URLSession`, a
bounded (default 256) LRU cache of decoded `NSImage`s / confirmed-404 `URL`s, in-flight de-duplication
per URL, and `nil` (never cached) for anything transient: a network error, a non-200/404 status, or an
undecodable 200 body. `AvatarView` drives it via `.task(id:)` keyed on the URL + the
`.loadRemoteAvatars` privacy gate (unchanged: no request issued while it's off). `AvatarImageFailures`
(the old error-blind, app-activation-cleared mitigation) is deleted — nothing else referenced it.
`AvatarImageLoaderTests.swift` covers it behind a `URLProtocol` stub: success/cache, genuine-404/cache,
transient-network-error/no-cache/retries, non-200/404 status, undecodable body, concurrent-request
de-dup, and LRU eviction — 7 tests, all green, no real network in any of them.

**Priority:** done.

### `FilesPanel` renders up to 4000 rows eagerly (macapp) — FIXED

**What:** `Views/FilesPanel.swift:58-60` builds every visible tree row in an eager `VStack`, capped at
`FileTreeModel.renderCap = 4000`, and each row holds `@EnvironmentObject store` + `@ObservedObject
model`.

**Measured (per this entry's own instruction), then fixed:** `FilesPanelInvalidationTests` added the
same `#if DEBUG bodyPasses` counter `HistoryRow`/`ChangedFileRow` use. Confirmed BOTH suspected
mechanisms on the pre-fix code: an `AppStore` publish saying nothing about the file tree rebuilt all
200 visible rows (`store` was read only inside tap/menu closures, never the rendered body — so this
was the WORKROOM-2B mechanism, not a hypothetical); a 1000-file tree built all 1000 rows on first
layout (the eager `VStack`).

Fixed the same way History/Changes were: `FileTreeRowView` now takes plain values + closures and
observes NOTHING (`FilesPanel` hoists `isExpanded` out of `FileTreeModel` per-row and passes
`onToggle`/`onOpenPreview`/`onOpenPersistent`/`onOpenInEditor`), gets an `Equatable` gate, and the
list is a `LazyVStack` — safe here (unlike `DiffViewer`'s soft-wrapping lines) since rows are
fixed-height and this already lives inside the inspector's own `ScrollView`. Re-measured: the
unrelated-publish case is now 0 rebuilds (was 200); the 1000-file tree now builds ~20-odd rows, not
1000; a 4000-file tree (the render cap) first-layouts in under the same 0.25s ceiling
`HistoryRowInvalidationTests` uses.

**Priority:** done.

### Use ghostty's native `theme = dark:<X>,light:<Y>` syntax (macapp)

**What:** Replace our rewrite-the-conf-on-every-appearance-change path with the engine's own
per-appearance theme selection.

**Why:** libghostty accepts `theme = dark:<X>,light:<Y>` and picks the variant itself. We instead
write a single `theme = "<name>"` and, on every appearance change, rewrite
`~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/ghostty.conf`, then `ghostty_config_load_file`,
`ghostty_app_update_config`, then `updateConfig` on every surface
(`GhosttyApp.swift` `writeThemeConfig`, `TerminalSessions.applyThemeToAll`). Muxy already uses the
native form (`muxy/Muxy/Services/ThemeService.swift` `parseThemeSelection`). Rolling our own where a
built-in exists is the finding.

**Pros:** deletes a hand-rolled apply path; removes the force-reload from every light/dark flip, which
is the most frequent theme operation there is.

**Cons:** the *chrome* still needs to know which variant is active, so `ThemeService.activeThemeName`
and its parse stay either way — the win is narrower than it first looks. Also couples us to a config
syntax the embedding C API doesn't version.

**How to start:** verify the pinned GhosttyKit accepts the two-variant form for new AND live surfaces
before committing (the pin is exact — see `project.yml`). Then `writeThemeConfig` emits both names once
and `applyThemeToAll` stops needing `force: true` on appearance changes.

**Priority:** P2 (removes a whole class of reload churn; no user-visible feature).

### Profile and fix the theme picker's invalidation storm (macapp)

**What:** Measure the picker's per-keypress cost, then stop every row re-rendering on every apply.

**Why:** `FamilyRow` holds `ThemeService.shared` and reads `theme.tokens`, while each ↑/↓ calls
`applyFamily`, which replaces `tokens` — so one arrow press invalidates every instantiated row. The
2026-08-06 change cached bundled theme previews, which removed the disk reads (up to 116 synchronous
file reads per keypress at 58 families) but **not** the re-render. This is the shape of the logged
WORKROOM-2B App Hang, and the repo already has the proven remedy: pass the needed values down instead
of observing the service, then `Equatable` + `.equatable()` on the row.

**Pros:** the remedy is known and cheap; arrow-browsing a 58-row list is now a real user behaviour.

**Cons:** the picker is a transient sheet, so the payoff is smaller than it was for `HistoryPanel`'s
200-row list. Measure first — the cache may already have made it imperceptible.

**Depends on:** the preview cache (landed 2026-08-06).

**Priority:** P3.

### Ship the remaining vetted theme families (macapp)

**What:** Three accessibility families — `GitHub Colorblind`, `Pierre`, `Adwaita` — and ten
same-family shade variants: Catppuccin Frappé + Macchiato, Tokyo Night Storm + Moon, Rosé Pine Moon,
Kanagawa Dragon, Gruvbox Hard, Modus Tinted, GitHub Dimmed, Nord Wave.

**Why:** all were swept against the real contrast floors during the 2026-08-06 expansion and came back
clean, so the measurement work is already done. The ten variants need only **one** new file each — the
light side already ships.

**Pros:** near-zero cost per family; accessibility is the one need in the recorded inclusion criterion
(`Resources/ghostty/themes/SOURCE.md`) that stays thinly served even after `GitHub High Contrast` and
`Xcode High Contrast` landed.

**Cons:** criterion rule 3 (distinct palette, not a shade of one we ship) argues *against* the ten
variants — they are exactly what that rule was written to exclude. Record that tension rather than
pretending the criterion endorses them. The a11y families' light sides are plain `#ffffff`.

**How to start:** re-run the sweep before shipping — upstream theme files move, and `themes/CHECKSUMS`
pins only what we already vendored.

**Priority:** P3.

             gate.settle(.failure(VCSCancellationError()))
             op.cancel()
           }
           Task {
             try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(max(0, seconds) * 1_000_000_000))
             gate.settle(.failure(VCSTimeoutError()))
             op.cancel()
           }
         }
       } onCancel: {
         cancelBox.fire()
       }
     }

The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

content.subject: Fix withTimeout not observing caller's own cancellation
content.description: TODOS.md line 608. Core/Timeout.swift's withCheckedThrowingContinuation only races its own internal deadline, never wires withTaskCancellationHandler, so it doesn't observe the calling task being cancelled externally. Wrap in withTaskCancellationHandler so cancelling the caller settles TimeoutGate early (same shape as JJSnapshotGate.run). Broad blast radius (WorkroomStatusResolver, BranchResolver, JJSnapshotGate's own use) - needs task #7's test harness in place first to verify the fix observably.
